id: # REPRESENTATION OF DATA TYPES - The Data Type Models in this Compiler

description: The compiler defines four distinct data representation models: (1) ABI representation for function calls, (2) SSA representation for MLIR operands, (3) Heap representation for runtime objects, and (4) Logical representation for Elm semantics
source: rules in one representation model do not imply rules in another unless explicitly stated

description: At all function call boundaries (kernel or compiled), every parameter and result whose monomorphized Elm type is Int, Float, or Char is passed and returned as a pass-by-value MLIR primitive (Int→i64, Float→f64, Char→i16), and every other Elm value including Bool and polymorphic type variables crosses the ABI as !eco.value regardless of its heap field representation
source: no ABI slot of type !eco.value may correspond to an Elm Int, Float, or Char.

description: SSA values of type !eco.value may denote either heap pointers or embedded constants, and codegen, GC, and runtime helpers must rely on the HPointer ptr_ind bit rather than pointer range checks to distinguish them (isConstantBits = ptr_ind != 0)
The comparable embedded constant is the merged Empty (word 0x6), which denotes "" for a String-typed comparison and [] for a List-typed comparison
source: it represents the minimum value of its type. Any compare/lt/le/gt/ge path that encounters Empty opposite a heap value of the same type must return LT for the constant-vs-heap case and GT for the heap-vs-constant case. When the type is String, Empty must additionally compare EQ against any heap String with header.size == 0 in any string form (Tag_String / Tag_StringSlice / Tag_StringRope / Tag_LargeStringHeader / Tag_StringUtf8View / Tag_StringUtf8Leaf). Well-typed Elm forbids comparing values of different types, so the merged Empty is only ever compared within a single comparable family.

id: # CANONICALIZATION PHASE - Resolve names, assign IDs, validate scopes

description: Every non-local variable reference in the canonical AST (top-level functions foreign imports constructors operators kernel vars) records its home module as an IO.Canonical so there is no ambiguity about which module a global name comes from while local variables are represented as VarLocal and resolved via the canonicalization environment

Every canonical expression node is assigned a unique non-negative integer ID ExprInfo.id by threading an Ids.IdState and calling Ids.allocId at each construction site and these IDs are later used as keys in the NodeTypes map returned by the type solver

No duplicate top-level value type constructor or port names exist in a module duplicates are detected via the Dups tracker and reported as DuplicateDecl DuplicateType DuplicateCtor DuplicateBinop or ExportDuplicate errors and shadowing of local bindings is likewise detected and reported as Shadowing

All imports must resolve to valid interfaces and all imported values types constructors and operators must come from those interfaces Foreign.createInitialEnv builds the environment from the given interface map and import list and unresolved or ambiguous imports yield canonicalization errors such as ImportNotFound ImportExposingNotFound or the various Ambiguous* errors

Module-level value definitions are partitioned into strongly connected components via Graph.stronglyConnComp this two-phase cycle detection (using all dependencies vs direct dependencies) ensures that groups used for type inference are valid recursive components and that non-terminating cyclic values are rejected with RecursiveDecl or RecursiveLet errors

Certain expression and pattern forms cache type information directly in the canonical AST to avoid interface lookups later in particular VarForeign VarCtor VarDebug VarOperator and Binop nodes carry cached Can.Annotation or Can.Type fields and constructor patterns PCtor and PatternCtorArg embed types for inference exhaustiveness checking and optimization

id: # TYPE CHECKING PHASE - Generate and solve constraints ensure type safety

description: In both erased and typed pathways type constraint generation traverses all declarations effects (ports and managers) expressions and patterns reachable from the module producing a single Constraint tree that encodes all required type relationships

Constraint solving uses union-find-based unification to compute consistent assignments for type variables and every unification failure produces a Type.Error (for example via Unify.AnswerErr and Error.BadExpr) that is propagated as a BadTypes error rather than silently corrupting the environment

After Solve.runWithIds completes every non-negative expression or pattern ID that was recorded during constraint generation has an entry in the nodeTypes dictionary (ExprTypes or NodeTypes) mapping that ID to a canonical type while negative placeholder IDs are intentionally skipped by the NodeIds.recordNodeVar helper

The occurs check implemented in Compiler.Type.Occurs is invoked by the solver during unification to detect and reject infinite types (such as a equals List a) and any such cycle results in a type error recorded in the solver state ensuring infinite types are never accepted

Let-bound type variables are ranked by lexical nesting depth using rank pools and generalization only quantifies variables at the appropriate rank promoting or freezing younger variables as needed thus implementing rank-based let-polymorphism and preventing unsound polymorphism from leaking across scopes

User-provided type annotations are canonicalized to Can.Annotation and inserted into the constraint tree the solver then enforces equality between annotated and inferred types so mismatches cause Type.Error values that surface as BadTypes errors rather than being silently ignored

In the typed constraint generator every type variable registered via NodeIds.recordNodeVar for an expression or pattern id must also appear in at least one constraint that participates in unification (either as the entire left or right side of a CEqual or nested inside a structured type that is unified)
source: a recorded variable that is only ever mentioned in NodeIds and never in any unification constraint indicates a missing constraint for that node and is treated as an internal compiler error
column7: Compiler.Type.Constrain.Typed.NodeIds|Compiler.Type.Constrain.Typed.Expression|Compiler.Type.Solve

id: # NITPICK PHASE - Pattern exhaustiveness and other semantic checks

description: Every case expression is exhaustive after the Nitpick phase meaning all possible values of the scrutinee type are covered by at least one pattern and any missing patterns are reported as InexhaustivePatterns errors so downstream phases can assume case expressions always match exactly one alternative at runtime

id: # POST-SOLVE PHASE - Fix remaining Group B types (Str, Chr, Float, Unit) and infer kernel function types

description: The PostSolve phase walks the canonical AST after solving and assigns structurally computed types to remaining Group B expressions (Str Chr Float Unit) whose solver types were unconstrained synthetic variables deriving these types from known concrete types. Most expression forms (List Tuple Record Lambda Accessor Let LetRec LetDestruct) are now Group A with solver-owned types via recordNodeVar and do not need structural repair

Kernel function types are inferred by a two-step process seeding the kernel environment from alias definitions whose bodies are VarKernel expressions and then propagating types from usages (direct calls constructor arguments binary operators and case branches) using one-way scheme-to-type unification to build a KernelTypeEnv that maps (home name) kernel pairs to canonical function types with first-usage-wins semantics

After PostSolve all non-negative expression IDs in NodeTypes have meaningful concrete types and no unconstrained synthetic type variables remain for non-kernel expressions so the fixed nodeTypes map is guaranteed to be suitable for building TypedCanonical and for downstream typed optimization

For remaining Group B expressions (Str Chr Float Unit) the structurally computed PostSolve types depend only on the canonical AST structure and the initial solver-produced nodeTypes so given the same canonical module and initial nodeTypes PostSolve deterministically produces the same fixed nodeTypes and kernelEnv

For every non-negative expression/pattern node id whose solver-produced (pre-PostSolve) type is not a bare Can.TVar PostSolve must not change that node type (alpha-equivalent) except for VarKernel nodes whose types may be inferred/filled during PostSolve

For every non-negative expression/pattern node id (excluding VarKernel and Accessor nodes) the set of free Can.TVar names appearing in the node post-PostSolve type must be a subset of those appearing in its pre-PostSolve solver type ensuring PostSolve does not introduce new polymorphism

Every lambda expression in the canonical module has a concrete structural function type. Lambdas are now Group A (solver-owned via recordNodeVar) so the solver provides their type directly. PostSolve verifies that the stored type is alpha-equivalent to the recomputed structural type (TLambda chain from argument pattern types and body type) so lambdas never remain as bare TVars or non-function shapes.

For every lambda expression the set of free Can.TVar names appearing in its post-PostSolve type must be a subset of the type variables available in its surrounding solver environment (from its pre-PostSolve node type or enclosing annotated scheme) ensuring that PostSolve does not introduce new unconstrained lambda-local type variables and that all lambda polymorphism originates from the main solver.

PostSolve-generated placeholder TVars used for structural repair of remaining Group B expressions (Str Chr Float Unit) must not appear in function positions in the fixed NodeTypes map for non-kernel expressions so that all function types visible to TypedCanonical TypedOptimized and monomorphization are expressed solely in terms of solver- or annotation-derived type variables and are free of PostSolve-only placeholders. Most expressions are now Group A and do not receive PostSolve placeholders.

For every non-kernel expression or pattern node id i, let EnvTVars(i) be the set of type variables available in i’s typing environment (the union of binders from all enclosing annotated or inferred type schemes, including generalized let-bound definitions) and let FreeTVars(i) be the set of Can.TVar names occurring in the final post‑PostSolve nodeTypes[i] type
source: the invariant is that FreeTVars(i) is a subset of EnvTVars(i), and any Can.TVar that remains in nodeTypes[i] but does not come from EnvTVars(i) indicates a leaked internal solver variable or placeholder and is treated as an internal compiler bug

id: # TYPED OPTIMIZATION PHASE - Preserve and exploit types in optimized IR

description: Every TypedOptimized.Expr variant carries its Can.Type as the last constructor argument and the typeOf helper function simply pattern-matches on each variant to return that trailing type field for any expression

All pattern matches are compiled into decision trees (Decider structures) that operate over flat variable bindings and destructor paths so no nested patterns remain in the TypedOptimized IR and the resulting Decider trees are exhaustive by construction relying on earlier pattern exhaustiveness checking and the decision-tree completeness guarantees

The typed local graph TOpt.LocalGraphData always includes the full Annotations dictionary mapping definition names to their type schemes carried over from type checking so monomorphization and backends can look up top-level types without re-consulting interfaces or re-running inference

Typed optimization is designed to be type-preserving transformations such as inlining dead-code elimination and case-to-decision-tree compilation construct new TOpt.Expr nodes whose attached Can.Type matches the inferred type from TypedCanonical or nodeTypes propagating types via local rules like function type equals argTypes arrow bodyType and call type equals peeled result type of the function

Function expressions in TypedOptimized carry their full function type as a list of (Name Can.Type) parameter types plus a result Can.Type and the overall expression Can.Type is the corresponding curried TLambda chain enabling accurate arity computation and type-directed specialization in monomorphization
Every TypedPath.Unbox segment in a typed decision tree is annotated with a concrete canonical wrapper type that corresponds to a single‑constructor union marked Can.Unbox and has a single field
source: this concrete Can.Type must be ground (contain no free Can.TVar) so that downstream phases can resolve a unique runtime wrapper shape for each Unbox path.
column7: Compiler.LocalOpt.Typed.DecisionTree|Compiler.AST.DecisionTree.TypedPath

id: # TYPED ARTIFACT SERIALIZATION - .ecot / typed-artifacts.dat wire format

description: On-disk .ecot and typed-artifacts.dat are a strict subset of the in-memory typed artifact. NOT serialized and rebuilt as inert defaults on decode: LocalGraph.main (Nothing) and LocalGraph.fields (Dict.empty) and GlobalGraph fields (Dict.empty) and ModuleTypeEnv.aliases (Dict.empty) and the per-Node deps sets of Define TrackedDefine Cycle Kernel PortIncoming PortOutgoing (EverySet.empty) and the Manager EffectsType (Cmd placeholder) and Kernel chunks and deps ([] and EverySet.empty) and Expr.VarDebug home and unhandledValueName (Elm Debug and Nothing). No consumer downstream of deserialization may read any of these fields. Adding such a reader requires re-adding the wire slot first and bumping typedGraphFormatVersion and V.compiler (ECOT_003 rule). Main detection on the typed path reads the in-memory TOpt main of Fresh modules and Details.Local.hasMain for cached ones, never a decoded main

Every .ecot section and typed-artifacts.dat graph or type env begins with a per-call string-table preamble: u8 index width (1 if count <= 256 else 2 if count <= 65536 else 4) then u32 count then count length-prefixed UTF-8 strings sorted ascending (Set.toList order) for bootstrap byte-identity. Every string field of the body and of the ECOT_003 type table is then the big-endian index of that width. For typed graphs the table is the body strings (collectStringsFrom* which skip type positions) united with the strings of the DISTINCT type-table entries (TypeTable.collectStrings) which is the same set as walking every type occurrence. A missing string is NOT caught: StringTable.string emits index 0 and the artifact silently mis-decodes. An extra string only grows the table but changes bytes. TOpt.computeVarSupers runs the same pre-pass (type table plus body collector in CollectSupers mode) so varSupers covers every emitted name including literals and fields. Interning is disabled (width 0 sentinel) for .eci and other legacy formats

From typedGraphFormatVersion 2 (V.compiler 0.1.2) every Can.Type in a typed graph body is written as a ref into a per-file type table that follows the string table: u8 ref width (1 2 or 4 by entry count) then the u32 entry count then the entries in id order. Refs are big-endian of that width. Dedup key = the full structural node under Elm == including the TLambda arrow slot and the FieldType index and Holey versus Filled alias bodies and the record extension name and alias argument names (the hash only picks a bucket and never decides equality). Ids are assigned children-first in first-occurrence order of the internTypesFrom* pre-pass so bytes never depend on the hash and every entry references only smaller ids. The decoder builds an Array in one forward pass and fails on a ref >= the entries decoded so far. Every type the encoder emits must have been interned by the pre-pass (TypeTable.ref crashes otherwise). Regions and zero-based indices and other non-literal Int fields in the body are LEB128 varints (uintV and zigzag sintV for the row delta). Int literals (TOpt Int expressions and decision-tree IsInt tests) are exact i64 as a signed 32-bit high word then an unsigned 32-bit low word (typedGraphFormatVersion 3 and V.compiler 0.1.3) because a float64 corrupted literals beyond 2^53 in cached modules. Any change to the table layout or key fields bumps typedGraphFormatVersion AND V.compiler because a failed package typed-artifacts.dat decode is silently replaced by an empty graph

id: # MONOMORPHIZATION PHASE - Specialize polymorphic functions to concrete types

description: MonoType encodes fully elaborated runtime shapes so concrete Elm instantiations of source types appear as MInt MFloat MList MTuple MRecord MCustom or MFunction and the only remaining use of generic type variables is via MVar with an attached Constraint such as CEcoValue or CNumber that does not require further type inference
At MLIR codegen time no MonoType may contain MVar with CNumber constraint in any reachable position and any such occurrence indicates a failed specialization compiler bug
Remaining MVar with CEcoValue constraint are allowed and their concrete source types never affect runtime layout or calling convention and are tracked only for comparison or debugging purposes
Every MonoNode whose MonoType is a function must be callable so it is either MonoTailFunc params body monoType or MonoDefine expr monoType where expr is MonoClosure closureInfo body monoType

Each specialization identified by Global plus MonoType plus optional LambdaId has a unique SpecId recorded in SpecializationRegistry every MonoVarGlobal that mentions that SpecId refers to exactly one MonoNode implementing that specialization and there are no missing or orphan entries in the registry for any used instantiation

RecordLayout and TupleLayout store fieldCount indices and a 2-bit-per-slot unboxedBitmap so field order indices and per-slot primitive kinds (00=boxed, 01=Int, 10=Float, 11=Char) for records and tuples are completely determined by these layouts (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)
Record field access computes fieldIndex and isUnboxed from the record MonoType layout so MonoRecordAccess and MonoRecordUpdate always use indices and unboxing consistent with RecordLayout

Function call specialization unifies canonical function types with monomorphic argument types so immediate numeric types are fixed to MInt or MFloat and immediate mismatches are treated as monomorphization bugs

Polymorphic Debug kernel calls keep type variables as MVar by applying an empty substitution so their MonoType stays polymorphic and those type variables always have CEcoValue constraint and do not affect runtime layout or calling convention
MonoGraph is type complete and contains every type in the program including all aspects of those types such as all constructors for custom types stored in ctorLayouts

MonoGraph is closed and hygienic every MonoVarLocal refers to a binder in scope every MonoVarGlobal and SpecId refers to an existing MonoNode and after applying the specialization-pruning pass (MONO_022) there are no unreachable specializations in the registry or nodes

For every function or closure node the function MonoType flattened arity (computed by recursively peeling nested MFunction layers e.g. MFunction [a] (MFunction [b] c) has flattened arity 2) is at least as large as the parameter list length and all call sites supply arguments not exceeding that flattened arity so full and partial applications are always well formed and closures returning functions (nested lambdas) are valid
For each custom type every constructor has a CtorLayout whose field count ordering and 2-bit-per-slot unboxedBitmap match the constructor's fields
source: all construction and pattern matching nodes that use that constructor are consistent with its CtorLayout (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot

description: After monomorphization every user-defined local function or lambda (non-kernel) that is reachable from MLIR codegen has no MVar with CEcoValue constraint in its MFunction parameter or result positions. Remaining CEcoValue MVar in those positions indicates a failed specialization. Enforced structurally by collectLocalCallSubst which derives concrete type variable mappings from call sites before specializing the local definition.

Reachable user-defined function and closure specializations MAY keep MVar with CEcoValue in their parameter result and capture types after monomorphization and at MLIR codegen entry: such a variable is a type variable nothing fixed (for example the element type of an empty-list argument or the field of a let-bound polymorphic record) and its value is always boxed and lowered as !eco.value so it changes no layout (see Mono.Constraint). The only forbidden residual type variable is MVar with CNumber: MONO_002 forbids it and Prune.pruneUnreachableSpecs closes it to MInt (MONO_028). The test checks MONO_002 over every node type expression type and parameter type of the monomorphized graph with a walk written independently of MonoTraverse (whose anyNodeType both closes and detects residuals in Prune). Supersedes the earlier rule that no CEcoValue MVar and no MErased may remain in user function types: MErased no longer exists in MonoType and CEcoValue residuals are by design.

After monomorphization and specialization-pruning every SpecId in SpecializationRegistry.mapping or MonoGraph.nodes is reachable from the main specialization via the callEdges graph. The reachable set is the least fixed point starting from mainSpecId (plus the port-decoder and flags-decoder roots) and following ALL MonoVarGlobal edges - a call a papCreate that names the spec and a bare reference stored into data are equally edges. No unused template specializations remain in MonoGraph. CtorShapes are also pruned to only include types referenced by reachable nodes. The pruned graph then carries ONLY the intra-SCC edges of that adjacency (self-loops included

description: MErased in MonoTypes that reach MLIR codegen (monoTypeToAbi monoTypeToOperand processType) is mapped to !eco.value (boxed). MErased arises from dead-value specializations (eraseTypeVarsToErased) and phantom type variables in polymorphic-key specializations (eraseCEcoVarsToErased). It is semantically equivalent to CEcoValue and is always lowered as a boxed eco.value at all boundaries.

For every specialization entry in SpecializationRegistry whose key MonoType is fully monomorphic (contains no Mono.MVar with CNumber or CEcoValue constraint and no MErased) and is reachable after specialization-pruning (MONO_022), a traversal of all MonoTypes reachable from its implementing MonoNode (including function parameter types, closure capture types, local binding types, and expression result types such as MonoLet, MonoCase branches, and intermediate nodes) must find no remaining Mono.MVar with CEcoValue constraint
source: any surviving CEcoValue MVar in such a context indicates either an incorrectly computed specialization key or a failure to propagate call-site or context constraints into the monomorphization substitution for that specialization.

description: For every reachable MonoClosure or MonoTailFunc node implementing a user-defined function or lambda specialization, the closure’s stored MonoType must be consistent with its specialization key: reconstruct the canonical function type from the specialization key MonoType and the top-level type environment, apply the monomorphization substitution used for that specialization, convert the resulting canonical function type to a MonoType (preserving TLambda staging), and assert that the flattened parameter and result types match the closure’s parameter list and result type (up to currying structure) so that closure parameter types, capture layouts, and return types are guaranteed to reflect the same concrete instantiation as the specialization key.

description: For StageCurried calls CallInfo.stageArities encodes the full stage segmentation of the callee's canonical function type as a non-empty list of positive integers.

description: MLIR codegen only inserts boxing and unboxing between immediate MLIR operand types and eco.value and any mismatch between different immediate MLIR operand types such as i64 versus f64 is treated as a monomorphization bug rather than fixed locally

generateDestruct and generateMonoPath always use the destructor MonoType to determine the path target MLIR type and never use the body result type so destruct paths yield their natural type and do not spuriously unbox
generateMonoPath projects heap fields into SSA operands: when the 2-bit slot kind in the heap layout is non-zero the result is an immediate SSA operand of the matching primitive type (i64/f64/i16)

Every eco.case is SSA value-producing: it has explicit MLIR result types on the op itself (not a result_types/caseResultTypes attribute), and every alternative region terminates with eco.yield whose operand arity and types exactly match the eco.case result types

description: Lambda functions use typed signatures where capture parameters have their actual MonoType mapped to MLIR types and return types match the body expression type rather than always using eco.value so no internal boxing or unboxing is needed for immediate captures and returns

eco.yield may only appear as the terminator of an eco.case alternative region and is forbidden in all other regions (including function bodies, joinpoint bodies, and SCF regions)

description: Generic-mode eco.papExtend (no remaining_arity attribute) is the generic apply operation. EcoToLLVM lowers it by building a typed i64* args buffer (no LLVM-side boxing of primitives) plus an EvalParamLayout describing each slot kind, then calling eco_apply_closure_typed. The runtime helper interprets the buffer per the layout (Int as i64, Float as bitcast f64, Char as zext i16, others as !eco.value HPointer) and is the single locus where any required re-boxing occurs

description: eco_apply_closure handles over-saturated calls by chaining per-stage evaluators. When num_args > remaining (max_values - n_values) it saturates the current stage then recursively applies remaining args to the result closure. The intermediate result is a closure for the next stage with its own n_values/max_values header. GC safety is maintained because intermediate results are held in C stack locals

CallInfo.callKind determines the MLIR call lowering strategy. CallDirectFlat is used for FlattenedExternal (kernels/externs). CallDirectKnownSegmentation is used for StageCurried calls where the callee closure has a traceable body with known staging. CallGenericApply is used for StageCurried calls where the callee is dynamic, has polymorphic return, or has unknown evaluator ABI (MonoVarLocal or other non-global/non-kernel callee). CallSegmentationUnknown is used for StageCurried calls where the callee has known evaluator ABI (global or kernel) and known monomorphic ABI types but untrusted staging (sourceArityInfo = FromType or hasUnknownExcessArgs) and the callee is not dynamic and does not have polymorphic return

For eco.papExtend with _call_kind = segmentation_unknown remaining_arity must be absent. EcoToLLVM lowers the op by building a single typed i64* args buffer (no LLVM-side boxing of primitives) plus an EvalParamLayout describing each slot's ParamKind, then calling eco_apply_segmentation_unknown. The runtime helper reads the closure header to determine saturation and dispatches: under-saturated calls go to eco_pap_extend with a 2-bit-per-slot bitmap derived from the layout
source: saturated and over-saturated calls forward to eco_apply_closure_typed which centralises any required primitive re-boxing. The LLVM IR for segmentation_unknown apply must not contain eco_alloc_int / eco_alloc_float / eco_alloc_char calls introduced solely to box arguments before the call.

id: # RUNTIME HEAP PHASE - Memory layout and GC invariants

description: Every heap object begins with an 8 byte Header struct and the first TAG_BITS bits of the header encode the Tag which denotes the concrete heap object kind
All heap objects are 8 byte aligned and getObjectSize always rounds object sizes up to a multiple of 8 bytes
GC and helper routines interpret heap object layout solely via Header.tag using a switch on the Tag enum in getObjectSize and related tracing functions
When introducing a new heap object type you must update the Tag enum the C plus plus struct definition getObjectSize scanObject and markChildren so all GC logic stays consistent with the Tag
There are no old to young pointers in the heap. The young generation is the nursery plus the young large-object space (HEAP_062)
source: both are traced by the minor GC. Guaranteed by Elm immutability and by the placement rule for large pointer-bearing objects (HEAP_062), so the GC does not require a write barrier. (Restored 2026-09-26, threaded-gc-04b

A tenure job's copies may point at YLOS objects of the tenured generation until the merge promotes them in place, and no mutator can reach those copies before the merge.

Every decision stays with the mutator.

id: # BYTES FUSION REIFICATION PHASE - Static analysis and fusion eligibility

description: Reification is all-or-nothing and a fused kernel is emitted only when the entire encoder or decoder structure can be statically resolved otherwise the interpreter path is used
Dynamic encoders and decoders are rejected from fusion and any encoder or decoder whose structure depends on runtime values causes fallback to the interpreter
Let-bound encoders and decoders are reified only if fully resolvable at compile time and partially resolvable let bindings cause the entire fusion to be rejected
Reification preserves operation order exactly so the sequence of encode or decode steps in the fused kernel matches the order specified in the source program
Reification inspects structure only and never runtime values so fusion decisions are based solely on the static shape of the encoder or decoder AST

id: # BYTES FUSION OPS PHASE - bf dialect IR and lowering invariants

description: Cursor is the only mutable state in fused byte operations and all state flows through cursor threading with no hidden side channels
Cursor is SSA-threaded so every bf operation that modifies cursor state consumes the old cursor and produces a new cursor value
Cursor pointer movement is monotonic and the pointer only moves forward never backward during encoding or decoding
Cursor end pointer never changes during execution and is set once at cursor initialization from buffer allocation
Cursor invariant ptr less than or equal to end always holds and any violation indicates a bounds check failure
Width computation is exact and equals the sum of all emitted write widths so buffer allocation matches total write size
Exactly one buffer allocation occurs per encoder invocation and all writes go to that single buffer
No writes occur after the buffer is returned and ReturnBuffer is always the final operation in an encoder
Write order is preserved exactly and bytes appear in the output buffer in the same order as the source program specifies
Writes never exceed allocated buffer size because width computation guarantees exact allocation
No intermediate buffers are created during encoding and all writes go directly to the final output buffer
No load occurs without a prior successful bounds check so all reads are proven safe before execution
Bounds safety is structural and enforced by IR shape so the bf dialect structure guarantees checks precede loads
Failure is terminal and decoding exits immediately upon any bounds check or semantic failure
Cursor does not advance on failure so failed decode attempts leave the cursor at the failure position
Semantic failures propagate as Nothing through the Maybe result type and never as exceptions or traps
Decoder never throws or traps and all error conditions result in Nothing return values
Successful fused decode produces results identical to the interpreter so fusion is purely an optimization

description: Directed set flow via content-carried deferred inclusions (plans/lss-directed-set-flow.md): LambdaSet gains LsFrom members sources - members-so-far plus DEFERRED in-edge source SLOT Points, meaning this slot INCLUDES each source slot, resolved at READ (pull-at-read: zonkSetSlot and zonkSigGo walk the reachable edge graph at that moment - no write hooks, no worklist, no batch pass, no barrier - read-time semantics inherit exactly HEAD's exposure). EVERY producer is lss.sigFlow-gated including the kernel-tunnel selector (the kernel boundary itself runs flag-off under LSS_021, so the gate lives at joinTunnels/joinKernelTunnels - without it the first PSFTunnels row would mint LsFrom flag-off) - flag-off no LsFrom exists and the representation is byte-inert. LsFrom's source list is NON-EMPTY by construction (addSlotSource only adds, merges carry sources through, top drops the whole variant - no collapse rule) - members may be empty (unlike LsMembers) - sources dedupe by raw pointKey at install and at the Unify join (IO.pointKey - Unify cannot import Engine) - top is absorbing and DROPS sources - EMPTY resolution reads LTop, never LSet [] (mirrors the FlexVar policy) - LsFrom never escapes the store (Mono.LambdaSetAnno stays LTop|LSet). Resolution is a one-pass DFS, visited keyed on raw pointKey and marked ON ENTRY (insert-after-descend loops on cycles), fresh per read, exact on cycles (union-over-reachables IS the least fixpoint: a visited hit contributes nothing, every SCC node's members are collected at that node, top short-circuits) - resolved values are NOT written back - later reads re-pull because sources may have grown. VARIANCE IS LOAD-BEARING: the directed walk flowArrowSets installs dst-includes-src only along FunL/Fun1 RESULT spines, FLIPS operands at ARG positions (contravariance - the double flip in nested arg positions is correctly covariant), and DEGRADES whole container subtrees (App1/Record1/Tuple1) to the symmetric join (per-parameter variance unknown - symmetric is the sound over-approximation - flowDegraded counts set-capable degrades). A directed walk that recursed arg positions covariantly would install wrong-direction edges and UNDER-approximate - the miscompile class - any new directed call site must re-argue variance. Defensive arms fail toward TOP, never toward skip/empty (dropping an edge under-approximates - the needSlow precedent defers to a SOUND slow path, ours writes top). The signature encoding is promote-or-internalize (the paper's Fig. 7 at the id level): zonkSigGo classifies each reachable node as another signature ordinal (PROMOTED into ArrowFact.sources, not descended - the caller-side edge delivers its members) or a non-signature slot (INTERNALIZED into members) - applyFactsGo installs slots[i] includes slots[j] per source ordinal as deferred edges, sound despite preceding arg unification BECAUSE resolution is deferred (the eager/snapshot FromArrow variant remains banned). Flipped sites: If/Case hub branch joins (branch INTO hub - the depollution: params keep their own singletons while the hub resolves the honest union, removing Run X's symmetric pollution), local-callee arg and result joins, kernel PSFTunnels under the selector. Kept symmetric: member-root, walkFunction result, Let/Def rhs, Let/TailDef result, joinLetUse (union-over-uses stays the let channel's v1 policy). Honesty rule unchanged: hubs publish only when every branch is honest - directedness fixes pollution, not blindness. Census: sigStats.edgesInstalled/flowDegraded, report-gated, on the sigflow: line AMENDED 2026-08-24: directed LsFrom flow was scheduled to retire with the arrow-identity work (plans/lss-unknown-elimination.md SS4.8 item 5), and it does NOT - item 5 is the terminal consumer of #6/#8/#9/#10, all of which need Phase 2b. It stays. Record for whoever revisits it: it was the right idea in a representation that could not carry it.

description: Kernel intrinsic annotations (plans/kernel-intrinsic-annotations.md): an Elm.Kernel.*/Eco.Kernel.* reference generates NO constraint by default (Can.VarKernel -> CTrue, Type/Constrain/Typed/Expression.elm), so a kernel is typed entirely by its context and one used INLINE rather than through an eta-free aliasing def is bounded by NOTHING - List.toArray behaves as alpha -> beta with the two sides never equated. source: absent a row the behaviour is unchanged, so the table is strictly opt-in per kernel. THREE RULES GOVERN A ROW. (1) The annotation is a REPRESENTATION claim, not documentation - solved types feed KernelAbi derivation and mono spec keys - and where the upstream JS type disagrees with the eco C++ the C++ WINS: List.fromArray/toArray are annotated List a -> List a, NOT the JS Array a -> List a, because in eco they are pass-throughs over cons lists (StringOps::split builds alloc::cons chains) and the JS type would make String.split's intermediate statically a four-field Array custom while dynamically a cons list. (2) It is FAIL-STOP, the inverse of a KernelSetFacts license: a wrong annotation is a TYPE ERROR in package code and the typechecker sees DEAD code too - elm/bytes 1.0.8's dead unexposed write helper calls Bytes.write_* JS-style against a C++ that builds 1-2-arg Encoder nodes, so that family is unannotatable without patching vendored source - hence every row carries useSites enumerating and verifying EVERY syntactic occurrence in every installed package (a closed set: kernel syntax is legal only in kernel-package source, Pkg.isKernel). (3) The key includes the PREFIX, unlike KernelSetFacts's (home,name) which genuinely collides on File.size - a license tolerates one row for both, an annotation cannot because the two types differ. Rows carry files pinned by sha256 in kernel-license-manifest.txt (the checker harvests this table alongside KernelSetFacts.elm). COMPOSES WITH LSS_022 IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: occurrence verification refuses licenses it cannot check and intrinsics supply the missing facts. Measured 2026-08-20 - (a) annotating fromArray/toArray/addEntry unblocked Inert license rows on the NEIGHBOURING kernels (String.split/join, Json.emptyArray) whose unsolved occurrence types had been failing isInertType, moving 4 and 2 boundaries from byKernel to kernelLicensed

description: eco_ensure_nursery_slow(n) (plans/capacity-check-hoisting.md) establishes bump_.end - bump_.ptr >= n for the calling thread WITHOUT allocating. Under HEAP_042's contiguous from-space, ensureHeadroom is a single comparison and a miss against the clamped end has exactly one meaning - the proactive-GC threshold tripped, or (under computeAllocEnd's already-full fail-soft) the extent is exhausted - so there is no block advance and no clamp-vs-exhaustion disambiguator to get wrong. Sequence: one minor GC, then the fail-soft unclamp to the full from-space extent (the tiny-config corner where threshold_total_bytes_ < n
source: unreachable at default config), then abort (HEAP_017). The SAME fail-soft rung is required in the three nursery allocation paths (ThreadLocalHeap::allocate / allocateSlow / allocateSlowRaw): a byte-exact clamp can leave less room below the threshold than the request needs, and collecting again cannot help because no allocation has happened since. n is a compile-time constant, 8-aligned, in (0,4096]. The guarantee is against the CLAMPED end, so the proactive trigger is fronted by <= n bytes
column7: it is VOID after any statepoint or any headroom-consuming leaf call. This is the SECOND exception to HEAP_011's may-trigger rule: unchecked bumps cannot GC, GC is confined to the run's ensure edge (the first exception is HEAP_034's per-construct diamond). Headroom is defined as 0 when bump_.end < bump_.ptr: ensureHeadroom compares ordered integers (end >= ptr && end - ptr >= n) and must never compute size_t(end - ptr) unguarded, which underflows to a huge value and would let a covered run bump unchecked past the extent
column8: a clamp below the bump pointer therefore means "must collect", the prerequisite for any future asynchronous safepoint doorbell (plans/threaded-gc-00-measure-and-fix.md Step 1, design_docs/parallel-gc.md §3.2)

description: Each NurserySpace semi-space is a SINGLE CONTIGUOUS EXTENT [base, base+capacity): the logical prefix of a fixed-size slice of the low or high nursery region, both slices at the same slot index (plans/contiguous-nursery-space.md M1). Slice geometry is min(nursery_max_block_count/2 * alloc_buffer_size, region per side) rounded down to an alloc_buffer_size multiple - CLAMPED to the region so a small heap gets one usable slot rather than a startup fatal - and is rebuilt by Allocator::rebuildNurserySliceTable at initialize() and reset(). capacity is ONE value per NurserySlicePair, so the two semi-spaces are equal by construction
source: it is quantized to alloc_buffer_size, bounded by min(slice size, the config's per-side max), and is the ONLY quantity GC semantics (membership bounds, threshold, growth, validators) may consult. A slot's physical retained_commit is allocator-private, monotone, per side, MAY exceed the current owner's capacity (dormant pages), is never re-commitAt'd (a MAP_FIXED re-map would discard the pages), is kept across releaseNurserySlicePair for Issue-#40 respawn reuse, and is DROPPED wholesale by Allocator::reset (slot bases move when alloc_buffer_size or the block caps change, so a stale record would skip committing pages that were never mapped at the new base). Consequences that are load-bearing: bump_.end = min(extent end, proactive-threshold trip) via computeAllocEnd with the already-full fail-soft, so a bump miss ALWAYS means minor GC - there is no block advance, no object that cannot straddle an interior boundary, and no abandoned tail gap
column7: growth extends both extents in place (or neither) and MUST re-derive the cached membership bounds before the next GC decision, or objects in the grown region are treated as non-nursery and never evacuated
column8: to-space evacuation is a pure bump, so the Cheney scan is scan_ptr_ < copy_ptr_, clearToSpaceFreeRegion is one memset, and the ECO_HEAP_VALIDATE pre-evacuation walk covers the ENTIRE allocated prefix instead of the current block only. Slot exhaustion is a loud fatal naming the sizing knobs threaded-gc-06 (HEAP_067/HEAP_068): during a parallel minor the to-space top is an atomic claimed by per-worker LABs, and the survivor prefix is then objects and Tag_Free fillers. threaded-gc-07 (HEAP_069): with nursery_regions = 1 a heap owns a region slice set instead of a pair: n extents (4, or 5 with eden flip) of ONE capacity, contiguous in its slot block at a power-of-two stride X (Allocator::acquire/grow/releaseNurserySliceSet, retained commit per extent). Growth extends all n or none, and contains() covers the whole slot block.

description: The old-gen/nursery address split is CONFIGURATION, not a constant (plans/contiguous-nursery-space.md M2): nursery_offset = max_heap_size - HeapConfig::nurseryRegionBytes(), computed once at the first Allocator::initialize (first init wins for the process lifetime - reset() re-derives slice geometry but never the region). nursery_region_bytes = 0 selects the default policy min(DEFAULT_NURSERY_REGION_BYTES, max_heap_size/2), which is 4 GiB of the 24 GiB default reservation (old-gen cap 20 GiB) and degrades to the legacy half split on heaps below 8 GiB so small test configs are unaffected. description: GC-free function propagation (plans/gc-free-function-propagation.md): a GENERATED function may carry gc-leaf-function ONLY when stamped by propagateGcFreeLeafAttrs, which runs once per module at the pre-RS4GC choke point in runEcoBackend - post-marker-expansion (get-tag, list-proj, list-cursor, inline-deref, expandInlineAllocs), post-$cap-prepass, pre-partitioning - so every RS4GC flavour (serial, deferred-after-opt, both split workers, single-partition inline) sees the attrs, which CloneModule and lazy deleteBody both preserve. (a) A function is stamped iff every call it can execute is accepted by llvm::callsGCLeafFunction (RS4GC's OWN per-call-site predicate, so the analysis cannot disagree with the pass) or targets another stamped defined function
source: poison propagates callee-to-caller to a fixed point and indirect calls, calls to non-gc-leaf declarations (every boxed eco_alloc_*, eco_alloc_inline_slow, eco_gc_alloc_region_slow, eco_list_tail_hybrid, eco_scratch_finish, eco_scratch_finish_fwd, dispatch helpers and every kernel extern EXCEPT the audited exception in clause (f)), interposable bodies and EH constructs are all poison. Do NOT reason by name prefix: the eco_alloc_*_fast / eco_init_*_at / eco_gc_alloc_region_fast family IS gc-leaf (null-on-miss, never collects). (b) Consequently no GC can begin while a stamped frame is on the stack, so calls to it need no statepoint and no relocation - the same contract the runtime gc-leaf helpers already rely on. (c) A stamped function that still contains a gc.statepoint after RS4GC is a HARD BUILD FAILURE (structural assert in runRS4GCAndMaybeFramePointers): RS4GC processes a body on hasGC() alone, so a callee's own gc-leaf attr does not stop it and the assert is a real check, not a vacuous one. (d) DELIBERATE EXCEPTION to the no-post-RS4GC-inlining rule: because calls to stamped functions stay plain calls, the post-RS4GC -O2 inliner can splice stamped bodies (including StripEcoCastBarriers-restored bare casts) into statepointed callers - sound because a stamped body holds no statepoint, so the inlined region lies strictly between the caller's statepoints whose relocations are already explicit SSA. description: EcoGCPrepare policy for gc-leaf kernels and inline-eligible allocation runs (plans/kernel-opt-09-gcprepare-barrier-relaxation.md). (a) FACT CHANNEL: the per-callee cannot-GC fact reaches EcoGCPrepare ONLY as the call-local UnitAttr eco.callee_gc_leaf, stamped by the module pass EcoMarkGCLeafCalls (Passes/EcoMarkGCLeafCalls.cpp, scheduled in buildEcoToLLVMPipeline immediately before createEcoGCPreparePass) by copying eco.gc_leaf from the is_kernel func.func declaration per CGEN_072(f). It MUST be call-local and MUST NOT be recovered by a symbol lookup at the consumer: the mirror consumer EcoGCLivenessAudit is a NESTED func::FuncOp pass and cannot see sibling declarations, and the two must agree bit-for-bit or validator builds report false positives on correct IR. Indirect calls and musttail calls are never stamped. The pass honours CGEN_072's ECO_KERNEL_GCLEAF=0 so that switch stays whole. ECO_GCLEAF_MARK=0 is its own bisect handle and ECO_GCLEAF_MARK_REPORT=1 prints the decl/site counts. (b) SAFEPOINT RELAXATION: a stamped eco.call is NOT a call safepoint - isCallSafepoint returns false and no root operand list is attached - and EcoGCLivenessAudit skips it identically, both through the single predicate gcLeafSafepointRelaxed() in Passes/EcoGCLiveness.h. DEFAULT-ON. ECO_GCPREPARE_LEAF_SAFEPOINT=0 restores rooting. This is an MLIR-ANALYSIS-ONLY change and is DISJOINT from CGEN_072(f): the root operands are split off at lowering by splitAdaptedRoots and handed to emitSafepointMarker, which is a no-op, so removing them emits no different LLVM IR - the real statepoints, spills and stackmap entries come from RS4GC reading gc-leaf-function on the callee DECLARATION. Do not double-count the two as one saving. Sound at MLIR level because Liveness is constructed once per function BEFORE any root operand is appended, so dropping call X's roots cannot perturb call Y's computed set. Pinned by the byte-identity gate: the produced eco-compiler is identical with the flag on and off. (c) NO GROUPING OF INLINE-ELIGIBLE RUNS: a run of adjacent fixed-size allocations whose members EVERY ONE has a call-free HEAP_034 inline singleton lowering (scalar BoxOp, ListConstruct, Tuple2/Tuple3Construct, and Record/CustomConstruct at <= 4096 bytes - AllocateCtorOp and AllocateStringOp are excluded, they have no inline path) is NOT grouped - it is broken into singletons before root computation so each member lowers through the ordinary inline bump. Grouping such a run is a PESSIMIZATION, not an optimization, for TWO reasons and the second is the stronger one. (i) Call count: a group lowers to an out-of-line eco_gc_alloc_region_fast call plus one eco_init_*_at call per member (lowerOneAllocGroup / emitInitAtPtr), where the same ops lowered individually make no calls at all. (ii) Capacity-hoisting interaction: the check-once-then-bump-many property groups were built for is now supplied at a LARGER granularity by CGEN_074 capacity-check hoisting, which covers a whole straight-line run of __eco_alloc_inline markers with ONE ensure diamond and turns every bump in it into an UNCHECKED bump - and eco_gc_alloc_region_fast is on that pass's isHeadroomBreaker list (EcoBackend.cpp), so every group flushRun()s and fragments the run. Grouping is also strictly weaker in reach: it requires adjacency AND no intra-group SSA dependency (consumesGroupMemberResult), which the Phase-1 census found blocks 98.1% of adjacent runs because the common shape is nested construction, whereas hoisting has neither restriction. Measured on a 9-allocation function: grouped = 4 space checks and 4 statepoints (3 eco_gc_alloc_region_slow + 1 eco_alloc_inline_slow) and is insensitive to hoisting because the group path bypasses the marker mechanism entirely - split = 1 space check and 1 statepoint (eco_ensure_nursery_slow). eco_init_*_at is gc-leaf and is never statepointed. The one case where grouping still gives fewer checks is a region hoisting cannot cover (external linkage, address-taken, CFG cycle, run > 4096 bytes): there the split costs one check per object - unmeasured, and the reason the kill switch exists. A run with ANY non-inline-eligible member keeps today's grouping - whitelist discipline. DEFAULT-ON. ECO_GCPREPARE_SPLIT_INLINE_GROUPS=0 restores grouping - also inert when ECO_INLINE_ALLOC=0. Pinned by test/codegen/gc_group_split_inline.mlir, which checks BOTH directions and is the first fixture the allocation-group path has ever had. (d) The Phase-1 census (ECO_GCPREPARE_CENSUS=1, counters in EcoGCPrepare.cpp) is the sizing evidence for all of the above and killed this plan's original group-MERGING transform outright: 98.1% of merge windows are blocked by a real intra-group SSA dependency and mergeableLeaf was exactly 0, so no motion transform exists here to relax a barrier for. Its windows column counts CROSSABLE windows only - hardBarrier is structurally 0 by construction, not a finding EcoGcFreePropagation (CGEN_072's MLIR producer) never writes eco.callee_gc_leaf.

description: Debug/bottom observable-ordering policy - full text design_docs/debug-log-ordering-policy.md. Any Elm-level pass that deletes duplicates merges or moves an expression must treat an expression transitively containing a Debug.* kernel reference as non-droppable non-mergeable and order-fixed. --optimize does NOT strip Debug on the MLIR path - checkForDebugUses (Builder/Generate.elm:259-266) is reached only from checkDebugAndGenerate (:195-198) under the JS prod entry (:188-192) and the native path Terminal/Make.elm:336/349/411/425 never calls it - so no pass may assume Debug absence. Debug.log lowers to eco.dbg (Generate/MLIR/Expr.elm:3921) and prints label: value into the captured program output stream via eco_dbg_print_typed. Bottom-selection latitude under --optimize permits keeping either of two crashing occurrences and the crash message may change. Pinned by test/elm/src/DebugLogOrderingTest.elm

Mono-level CSE (Compiler.GlobalOpt.MonoCse, kernel-opt-13, DEFAULT-OFF, ECO_CSE=1) may merge two occurrences of an expression only when ALL of: (a) PURITY - CsePurity.isSafeExpr accepts it, i.e. every kernel it names is KernelFacts cseSafe and every global callee is in the transitive observation-free set. Debug is unsafe by construction, which is how OPT_DEBUG_ORDER_001 D-2 is enforced here rather than by a separate test. (b) DISTANCE - at least one occurrence's path from the lowest common ancestor is entirely unconditional, so that occurrence is evaluated on every path reaching any other and binding at the LCA speculates nothing. A group whose suffix enters a closure body is excluded PERMANENTLY (different evaluation frequency), not deferred. (c) SCOPE - no free local of the candidate may be bound BELOW the LCA. This is a scope test, not a shadowing test: a local bound between the LCA and an occurrence is in scope at the occurrence but not at the binding site. The binder list must include MonoTailDef PARAMETERS as well as MonoLet and MonoDestruct names - omitting them hoists a candidate above its parameter's binder and produces lookupVar unbound-variable. (d) NON-OVERLAP - the let binds the ORIGINAL first-occurrence subtree verbatim, so no kept group's occurrence subtree may contain or be contained by another kept group's. (e) NOT function-typed (CGEN_069: a hoisted function-typed value invalidates the enclosing call's staged CallInfo) and containing no binder or closure. The pass MOVES the first occurrence and DELETES the duplicates - it never copies, so binder multiplicity strictly decreases and the inliner's freshenLetBoundNames hazard does not arise. It runs in Builder.Generate.runGlobalOptPhase AFTER globalOptimizeWithStats and BEFORE CafDedupe: it adds MonoLet bindings and annotateCallStaging is O(2^let-depth), so running it pre-annotation would re-arm that exponential. Any path encoding used to locate occurrences MUST give distinct decider leaves distinct keys - a Chain/FanOut tree whose Leaf Inline nodes share one step makes two occurrences collide, which both inflates the census and produces a MonoLet that does not dominate its uses. NaN-SHARING HAZARD (discovered 2026-08-13 via MLIR CSE, ContainerEquality*FloatTest): merging two evaluations of an expression whose runtime value can transitively contain a Float leaf is OBSERVABLE - the equality kernel's pointer-fast-path answers True on the shared object where the NaN-aware structural walk answers False - so before this pass is ever enabled it MUST additionally refuse candidates whose result type can reach a Float, and the same restriction applies to any future widening of the MLIR-level eco.cse_safe merge licence

TAG PROVENANCE IS UNIFORM AND MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: MonoEnum is minted as CtorTag.effective ... (Specialize.elm, solver twin MonoSolver/Monomorphize.elm) and CtorShape.tag comes from CtorTag.effective (Monomorphize/Analysis.elm), so applying CtorTag.effective a second time at emission is a latent bug a future reserved-tag addition would detonate. ORDER MATTERS in all three: the null-cons test comes FIRST, because the legacy chain falls through to the Bool arm for any non-Empty constant and would read a null-cons word as True. In the two open-coded forms the derived index (lshr+and off the ptrtoint) MUST be computed in the SAME basic block as the ptrtoint - REP_LLVM_001(d)'s same-BB bit-test acceptance - and only the derived i64 crosses into the embedded-constant block. description: PLATFORM BOUNDARY IS ALL-BOXED FOR THE MODEL (fixed 2026-08-25, plans/task-perform-value-msg-segfault.md). Platform.worker's init and update both return ( model, cmd ) as a Tuple2, and a Tuple2 carries its slot kinds in header.unboxed - 2 bits per slot, 00 boxed HPointer / 01 Int / 10 Float / 11 Char - so for an UNBOXED model type (Int/Float/Char) slot a holds a RAW SCALAR, not a pointer. PlatformRuntime::initWorker and the update path MUST read that slot through Elm::alloc::boxElement(slot, kind) and never as a bare .p. Reading .p reinterprets the scalar as an HPointer and breaks TWO invariants at once: the word is stored into modelStorage_ which is then handed to eco_gc_add_value_root, violating HEAP_035 (a slot holding a raw scalar must NEVER enter the root set), and the first callClosure1(subscriptionsFn, model) resolves it - Allocator::resolve on a raw i64 - and SIGSEGVs. Confirmed under gdb: init _ = ( 1, .. ) produced model = {constant=0x1, ptr_ind=0x0, ptr=0x0}, i.e. the raw 1 with ptr_ind CLEAR so it is not a valid embedded constant either (HEAP_010). The boundary is all-boxed in BOTH directions - callClosure1/2 pass the model back to Elm through the all-boxed arg layout - so boxing here is the contract, not a workaround. boxElement ALLOCATES for an unboxed kind and can move the tuple, so each site re-resolves the pair before reading slot b. WHY IT HID: every pre-existing worker fixture used a model that really is a pointer or a tagged constant (TimerEffectTest a record, MVarSharedNewTaskTest a Maybe). Gated by test/elm/src/TaskPerformValueTest.elm and TaskAttemptErrorTest.elm - an Int model is the point of those fixtures, do not 'tidy' them into records

description: FAST-EVALUATOR SYMBOL PROVENANCE (fixed 2026-08-25, plans/lss-paper-inclusion-constraints.md SS5.A1). A monomorphized node whose ENTIRE expression is a MonoClosure - an ordinary top-level `f a b = ...` - is emitted by Generate/MLIR/Functions.generateNode under specIdToFuncName registry specId, the SPEC's name - its own closureInfo.lambdaId NEVER becomes an MLIR symbol. Only Lambdas.elm, which emits NESTED closures, names anything lambda_NNN. AbiCloning.collectGo did not draw that distinction: it indexed EVERY MonoClosure under closureInfo.lambdaId, so when a top-level instance won a LayoutGroup rep election StampPap wrote fastEvaluator = Just inst.lambdaId and Expr.elm rendered it with lambdaIdToString - naming a function that was never emitted. PapExtendOp::verifySymbolUses (runtime/src/codegen/EcoOps.cpp) is what catches it, as `'eco.papExtend' op references undefined fast evaluator`. THE CONTRACT: any stamp that will be rendered as a SYMBOL must record which emitter owns the instance, never re-derive the name from the lambdaId alone. Mono.CallInfo.fastEvaluatorSpec : Maybe SpecId carries that provenance - AbiCloning.collectInstances threads the node's SpecId through its fold and collectNode hands it to the node's TOP-LEVEL closure only, for EXACTLY the three node kinds that route through Functions.generateDefine - MonoDefine, MonoPortIncoming, MonoPortOutgoing - since those hand their whole expression to generateClosureFunc funcName. MonoTailFunc is deliberately EXCLUDED: its params are already split out and its expr is the BODY, so a closure sitting there is an ordinary nested lambda that Lambdas.elm names, and attributing the spec to it would swap one wrong symbol for another. Nested closures everywhere get Nothing, unchanged - Instance.topLevelSpec is set ONLY when closureInfo.captures is EMPTY, because generateNode emits the spec un-suffixed and the spec name is therefore usable only where the emitter takes the bare branch rather than `...$cap` - a top-level definition is closed over globals so this is expected to hold universally, and the guard makes a violation degrade to the OLD loud lowering error rather than invent a wrong $cap symbol. Expr.elm's stamp carries FastRef = ( LambdaId, Maybe SpecId ) and fastRefBaseName resolves it. TWO PLACES THAT SILENTLY UNDO IT IF FORGOTTEN: (a) MonoGlobalOptimize's stamp-PRESERVING record update must copy fastEvaluatorSpec alongside fastEvaluator, or a later rewrite drops the provenance back to the lambdaId spelling - (b) GlobalOpt/MapTemplate renders its callee with lambdaIdToString and therefore DECLINES any site whose fastEvaluatorSpec is Just. MEASURED on the self-compile: 17 stamps are both top-level and stamped with lss.arrowSolverRoots=1 and ZERO at shipping defaults - which is exactly why LSS_031 being default-off hid this - and 25,486 top-level closures carry 25,486 DISTINCT uids, so no lambdaId collision was ever involved. BYTE-NEUTRAL AT DEFAULTS BY CONSTRUCTION: with roots off nothing sets topLevelSpec, fastEvaluatorSpec is always Nothing, and every emitted symbol is character-for-character what it was. GATED 2026-08-25: self-compile with ECO_MONO_LSS_ARROW_ID=1 ECO_MONO_LSS_ARROW_ROOTS=1 emits EXIT=0 (15,054,203 B of MLIR) and LOWERS EXIT=0 (70,450,536 B binary) with ZERO 'undefined fast evaluator' errors - the only ld output is the pre-existing stackmap-relocation / DT_TEXTREL warning pair. GATE RULE THIS INHERITS FROM LSS_031: a change to lambda-set IDENTITY must be gated on a SELF-COMPILE LOWERING, not on E2E - E2E passed 1687/1687 with the bad stamp because its corpus is small programs

THE SHADOW-Q VERIFIER (plans/lss-paper-inclusion-constraints.md SS5.1/SS5.6). Flag lss.qCensus, env ECO_MONO_LSS_QCENSUS, hash token lssQC=, DEFAULT-OFF and SPLIT FROM lss.report on 2026-08-26 - it used to ride the report flag, and the benchmark protocol in benchmarks/lss-opt.md MANDATES ECO_MONO_LSS_REPORT=1, so every timed run was paying for ~106k recorded constraints per compile plus a solve and a reachability walk per inference unit, inside the measured wall/RSS/GC. THE PROPERTY IT GUARDS, and it is the reason this is a verifier rather than a census to read once: EVERY PATH THAT PUTS A MEMBER IN A SLOT MUST BE A RECORDED CONSTRAINT. Q records `l <= sigma` at exactly two sites - Store.unifySlotWithSetC (every member and top write) and Store.addSlotSource (LSS_023 edges, as sigma_dst >= sigma_src) - captures each target slot's content BEFORE the write (the eager answer is seed join Q, and without the seed an annotation-minted slot reads as a spurious divergence), groups by UF.repr at the boundary so two slots the solver unified are ONE sigma exactly as they are one variable in the paper, solves the least fixpoint, and scores it against the store. READ-ONLY: the threaded store is dropped and only counters cross the boundary, exactly as Store.rezonkSettled is read-only (LSS_035) - if that ever changes the verifier becomes a behaviour change wearing a verifier's clothes. WHICH ARM IS GATED: `Q-infer:` is scored inside LssInfer.inferUnitInScratch over the unit's own signature roots, which is where the paper's Q lives, and its REPRODUCES=yes is the gate - MEASURED 2026-08-26 at 0 divergences over 106,300 classes, which is the empirical proof of the fidelity mapping's asserted claim that Eco's eager solving computes the paper's minimal solution S(Q,alpha). `Q-shadow:` scores the SPECIALIZATION phase at finishNode and is NOT gated, because two routes legitimately diverge there and both are the paper's own design rather than defects: (a) a spec's stored demand type re-enters the store as GROUND via Translate.demandUnifyVar -> Store.monoTypeToVar, which is the paper's sigma-bar (Fig. 9 Mono-Used) - the paper has ground sets at specialization too, what it does NOT have is constraints there, because Q is discharged when inference ends - and (b) Store.monoTypeToVarC mints a slot already holding an LSet or LTop annotation, so those members enter without a write and are invisible to Q. Measured 66 of 110,090 classes at that scope, all shadow-subset-of-eager, split 44 unseen / 12 known-elsewhere / 10 at top. A REPRODUCES=NO on the INFER line is a genuine defect and means a new write path bypasses unifySlotWithSetC - the same class of self-check as LSS_030's RECONCILES field. TRAP that cost two false readings while this was being built: the log holds Points and is STORE-SCOPED like arrowMemo/arrowOfSlot/zonkLog, so it MUST be cleared by clearedAux and restored by restoredAux on every scratch-store swap, and it is consumed and cleared at the inference boundary so the two censuses PARTITION the constraints rather than one silently eating the other's (scratchDropped fell 106,023 -> 0 when that landed, and the recorded edge count went 0 -> 177, matching sigflow's independent counter exactly)

description: Closed-world output (an executable, or an object built with --internalize-keep) is erased and internalized in MLIR by EcoReachability (plans/mlir-split-backend-03-reachability.md), placed directly after EcoTailConversions and before the capacity and gc-free planners: every symbol op not reachable from the roots (main and __eco_init_globals, or the keep list with eco_main spelled main) is erased - definitions, globals and declarations, GlobalDCE semantics - and every reached non-root definition with External linkage becomes Internal, recorded as the module flag eco-reach. Edges are EcoSymbolGraph's (an unused llvm.mlir.addressof is no edge, refs held by non-symbol top-level ops are roots). No post-translation step may add a reference to a generated definition and marker expansions reference runtime symbols only, so the LLVM side keeps only a removeDeadConstantUsers sweep (finishReachability) plus, under ECO_REACH_VALIDATE=1, the old internalize + GlobalDCE as an oracle that must remove nothing and relink nothing. __eco_root_module is baked only for .so/.node output. ECO_REACH_MLIR=0 restores the LLVM internalize + GlobalDCE

Constant-thunk folding (plans/mlir-split-backend-04-constant-thunks.md) is a codegen perf layer like nullConsBySpec / constCtorBySpec: ConstThunks.build admits arity-0 MonoDefine specs (never main) whose body is a literal other than String, Unit, a kernel float constant (pi, e), or an alias chain ending at one of those or at a null-cons / Nothing constant (phase 1, constThunks >= 1), or - phase 2A, constThunks = 2, the default - a closed body of those plus lets and saturated calls lowering to a pure non-allocating arithmetic intrinsic (both the MonoVarKernel and the elm/core global routes, plus kernel logBase) within 24 nodes. generateVarGlobal emits the thunk's OWN body at the reference instead of the eco.call, under a fresh lexical scope (varMappings, currentLetSiblings, externBoxedVars, splitAggParams, decoderExprs, fwdRefdLetNames, tailRecLetBody and sretTailLayout reset and restored, accumulators threaded, definedSsaVars kept), then coerces to the thunk's ABI return type, so values, poison and guard semantics equal calling the thunk. The thunk's func.func is unchanged and still returns the same value for any path not routed through the map. Env ECO_CONST_THUNKS=0|1|2 (hash token cthk=N), census ECO_CONST_THUNK_REPORT=1. EcoSplit (plans/mlir-split-backend-05-ecosplit.md): with EmitObjectFile output, parallel-opt cgu or dev, -O>0, no rs4gc-after-opt, a multithreaded MLIRContext, ECO_MLIR_SPLIT not 0 and the shared partition policy giving N > 1, the final llvm-dialect module is partitioned in MLIR instead of translating one llvm::Module - LPT ownership on MLIR op counts, globals at the owner of their first referrer, $cap import copies cloned as available_externally (the Call-bit closure into $cap bodies owned elsewhere, only when the $cap prepass will run), declarations cloned with ALL attributes for every other referenced symbol, llvm.module_flags cloned into every partition plus eco-list-chunks for the one whole-module expansion gate (the get-tag Tag_ConsChunk compare, whose eco_enable_list_chunks call lives only in main). EcoSplit hard-errors in release builds when any declaration or copy does not carry exactly its owner's eco-cap-* facts (01 S6). Each partition is translated on its own thread into its own LLVMContext and lowered by runEcoBackend in partition-worker mode (splitEligible true, splitCodegen 1, own TargetMachine): owned functions referenced from another partition become External + hidden before the $cap prepass, import copies are dropped back to declarations right after it (unconditionally), every local is externalized after the gc-free finish, and no available_externally function may reach RS4GC (hard error, all modes). Whole-module validate twins (01 compute mode, 02 gc-free twin, 03 DCE oracle and address-taken cross-check) are bypassed per partition and run on the translate-whole path (ECO_MLIR_SPLIT=0). Diagnostic files written by workers get a .p<i> suffix. The (X) gc-leaf join runs over the workers' reports. Function bodies equal the translate-whole path's modulo phi incoming order B4 (plans/mlir-split-backend-06-partition-boundaries.md): an owned $cap with no Address or CallMismatch in-edge is exported by its owner only AFTER the prepass and only if it survived it - the prepass mark is computed identically on identical bodies in every partition, so when the owner's AlwaysInliner deleted the body every importer inlined its copies too - and the driver hard-errors if an importer kept a marked copy of a body its owner deleted. Every function body equals the translate-whole path's modulo phi incoming order, with no extra functions.

description: OLD-GEN BLOCKS HAVE STABLE IDS AND METADATA STORAGE NEVER MOVES (plans/threaded-gc-01-stable-metadata.md, 2026-09-24). Every old-gen block has a BlockId assigned by BlockTable::add (OldGenSpace::materializeBlock is the one entry point) and stable until the block is released - ids are recycled LIFO only after release. The block's BlockInfo, BufferMetadata, large-mark byte, MarkBitArena slot and LiveBytesAccumulator entry live at fixed addresses: all storage is ReservedArray, VA-reserved at OldGenSpace::initialize for max_blocks = old-gen reservation (Allocator::getOldGenReservationBytes = nursery_offset) / alloc_buffer_size + 1, committed on demand, and never reallocated or moved (OldGenSpace::geometryFor - 8 TB reserves ~130 GB of VA per heap and costs memory only for used ids). Iteration ORDER (BlockTable order) is distinct from identity and reproduces the former std::vector<BlockInfo> exactly, including swap-remove on release and order-preserving erase in compaction, because lazy-sweep order, first-fit reuse and reclaim order depend on it. Only loop variables and the two cursors sweep_buffer_index_ and fixup_buffer_index_ are positions - every other stored block reference (mark-stack entries, free_large_blocks_, evacuation_set_, evac_block_index_, page-index owners) is a BlockId (a struct with no implicit integer conversion). Only the owning heap's mutator thread releases blocks or recycles ids, at points where no GC work item holds an id. large_body_index_, free_large_blocks_, unassigned_blocks_, free_lists_ and the mark stack are owner-only. ECO_HEAP_VALIDATE re-derives the order/pos bijection, stored-reference liveness and storage stability at every major GC, release batch and 64th minor GC. Each id carries a generation (BlockTable::generation, a monotone ReservedArray<uint32_t> gen_), incremented at every materialization (BlockTable::add) and never reset (clear() keeps it), so a same-id re-issue is a distinct incarnation (CR-036, 2026-09-30: IM5 keys on it). BlockInfo stays 40 bytes.

THE OLD-GEN PAGE INDEX COVERS THE WHOLE RESERVATION AND IS NEVER REBUILT (plans/threaded-gc-01-stable-metadata.md). Slot = (p - heap_base) / alloc_buffer_size over [heap_base, heap_base + nursery_offset) - VA-reserved at initialize, committed through region_end_ wherever region_end_ grows (OldGenSpace::commitPageIndexThrough, also from Allocator::ensureOldGenCapacityFor), and maintained incrementally: assigned at materialize, cleared before release on BOTH removal paths (releaseBlockToAllocator and compaction's freeEvacuatedBuffers). A region-bounds change only recomputes region_base_/region_end_. A slot has at most two owners because every block is >= alloc_buffer_size (a third is a validator abort). Owners are stored as BlockId.v + 1 so a fresh zero-filled slot means empty. blockIdFor keeps the region-bounds early-out and MUST bounds-check the slot against the committed count (uncommitted slots are PROT_NONE) - it has no linear fallback. threaded-gc-05c (HEAP_065): background markers read the index while the owner adds blocks, so owner words are stored with release (storeOwner) and loaded with acquire (loadOwner) after materializeBlock has written the BlockInfo and mark slot. ReservedArray committed counts are atomics (release after the commit syscall, acquire on read) and the region bounds are relaxed atomics written only through setRegionBase/setRegionEnd (recomputeRegionBounds included, CR-009) and read only through regionBase/regionEnd (during a cycle the region only grows). The single writer's own reads of the bounds and of owner words also go through atomic_ref (regionBase/regionEnd, loadOwnerRelaxed - relaxed, plain moves on x86) because markers may hold an atomic_ref to them ([atomics.ref.generic]/3, CR-021).

OLD-GEN MARK BITS LIVE IN A FIXED PER-ID ARENA SLOT (plans/threaded-gc-01-stable-metadata.md). Block id's bitmap (1 bit per 8-byte slot) is at arena + id * stride with stride = round_up(alloc_buffer_size / 64, 64) and a per-id valid length (bitmap bytes for a regular block - 0 for is_large and free ids, whose liveness is the BlockTable large-mark byte). The `byte_index >= len` guard is load-bearing. MarkBitArena::assign zeroes a slot whenever an id is (re)materialized - drop() zeroes it on the flip to is_large - retire() empties it on release. startMark (MarkBitArena::clearForMark) zeroes EVERY live slot and live large-mark byte - the bulk clear is load-bearing because a set bit can survive a block sweep walked to completion (gc-opt-loop W11b) - then discards runs of free-and-dirty slots to return their RSS. There is no re-pack and no per-block offset table. The arena is a 2 MiB-aligned ReservedArray committed and discarded in whole 2 MiB granules so it stays eligible for transparent huge pages (4 KiB pages measured ~1 % slower on mark). clearForMark also runs at t0 of an incremental mark cycle (HEAP_063, OldGenSpace::prepareMark shared by startMark and beginMarkCycle). With parallel marking (HEAP_064) the bits and large-mark bytes are set by atomic fetch_or / exchange (std::atomic_ref, relaxed: the bit only arbitrates who scans). threaded-gc-05c (HEAP_065): during a cycle, mutator allocate-black on the non-cursor paths (mixed pops, splits, bag pages, large blocks) is an atomic fetch_or / store (setMarkBitAtomic) because a background marker may set other bits of the same byte. The cursor (finalizeBitmapCell) keeps its plain bit set because mid-cycle it owns only blocks created after t0 (validator IM13).

MARKING ATTRIBUTES LIVE BYTES ONLY TO A LIVEBYTESACCUMULATOR (plans/threaded-gc-01-stable-metadata.md). markOneObject adds the object's walk-step bytes to the marker's LiveBytesAccumulator (indexed by BlockId), never directly to BufferMetadata::live_bytes - the allocator side (allocate-black in initObjectHeaderWithSize, the large-block reuse paths, freeLargeBodyCell) writes only BufferMetadata. The accumulator is merged into BufferMetadata::live_bytes as the FIRST action of finalizeMetaAfterMark (the mark->sweep sync point), before any post-mark reader, and is all-zero outside [resetBufferMetaForMark, merge] (validator-checked). Marking is stop-the-world and both writers only add, so the merge is exact - freeLargeBodyCell's clamped subtraction folds that id's entry first when marking_active. Phase 4 gives each marker thread its own accumulator, merged at the same statement. During an incremental mark cycle (HEAP_063) allocate-black writes only BufferMetadata::live_bytes, the accumulator's sum at the handoff is the cycle's traced live (threaded-gc-05a). threaded-gc-05b (HEAP_064): one LiveBytesAccumulator per marker (OldGenSpace::MarkWorker::live), merged in index order at finalizeMetaAfterMark (markLiveMergeAll), V5 checks every marker's accumulator. Validate builds check it twice: all-zero right after markLiveMergeAll (2026-09-29
source: a skipped merge before a run's last cycle was otherwise never seen) and again at the next mark start. The allocator side writes BufferMetadata in EVERY phase (HEAP_073, CR-018, 2026-09-30), atomically while a parallel promotion is active (par_promo_active_) or the cell is allocated black. The S1 half of CR-001 (a stash cell finalized at Idle left uncounted) is closed by HEAP_073
