description: OLD-GEN FREE-LIST BACK-LINKS ARE ADDRESSES (plans/threaded-gc-01-stable-metadata.md). A Tier-M free cell's class-list predecessor is encoded as its address >> 3 (40 bits - heap addresses are < 2^43): the low 32 bits in FreeCellMid::prev_lo and the high 8 bits in Header.refcount[0,8) of the SAME Tag_Free cell, with refcount bit 8 marking the head of its class list. Header.refcount is otherwise unused on Tag_Free cells - only setPrevHead / setPrev / copyPrev (OldGenSpace.hpp) write these bits, and getPrev decodes them without reading block metadata. Tier-M threading requires only a block context, not a bounded block count (the former {16-bit block index, offset} CellHandle capped it at 65,535 blocks and silently disabled threading above). Validator V6 checks every back-link against the actual predecessor.

COLLECTION CODE READS PER-HEAP STATE, NEVER THE CALLING THREAD'S TLS (plans/threaded-gc-01-stable-metadata.md). A heap's collection code reads that heap's own state: nursery membership through OldGenSpace::nursery_ (bound by the ThreadLocalHeap constructor - not Allocator::isInNursery, which resolves tl_heap_), the in-minor-GC flag (OldGenSpace::in_minor_gc_ / NurserySpace::minor_gc_running_, set and cleared by NurserySpace::minorGC - formerly thread_local g_in_minor_gc) and the batch-release depth (OldGenSpace::batch_release_depth_). Thread-local state is allowed only for mutator-only state (eco_tl_bump_state, eco_tl_root_*, the ListScratch stack, the unwind context) and for per-worker validator diagnostics (g_scan_parent/tag/size, g_push_origin, g_first_push_origin). ECO_HEAP_VALIDATE asserts the bound nursery agrees with tl_heap_'s on the mark path.

UNIFORM OLD-GEN BLOCKS ALLOCATE FROM THEIR MARK BITMAP (plans/threaded-gc-02-bitmap-allocation.md, 2026-09-25). With HeapConfig::old_gen_bitmap_alloc, a uniform block's mark bitmap is its allocation map: a cell-start bit is set <=> the cell is allocated (live at the last mark, or allocated since). Uniform blocks are never lazily swept: classifyBlocksAfterMark (every finishMarkAndSweep overload, after reclaim/shrink, before recomputeSweepPendingBlocks) marks them fully_swept and queues each partially free one on partial_[class] in position order. Per class one AllocCursor owns at most one block (BlockInfo.alloc_state Current) and scans its bitmap with bitscan::nextFreeCell, setting the bit on allocation - cursors and queues are reset at startMark. A block is detached (detachFromAllocation) before it is released, flipped to large, demoted or compacted. A uniform block's live_bytes equals popcount(cell-start bits) x cell_bytes outside the mark window (validator V8). Virgin blocks (unsliced, all-clear bitmap) replace populateFromBlock at exactly its ladder rungs - never above a reuse rung (the W6 rule). Demotion to mixed happens iff live_bytes <= HeapConfig::demote_live_fraction x totalBytes (default 0.3, chosen by experiment E1 - plan §9 item 9 - 0.5 is the former live*2 <= total), and 0.0 disables demotion entirely (an explicit early return). One owner per block is the promotion-buffer shape threaded-gc phase 6 extends to one cursor per thread. The bitmap is the allocation map OUTSIDE a mark cycle: during an incremental cycle (HEAP_063) the bitmaps of blocks that existed at t0 hold mark bits only (clearForMark erased the allocation record), so no allocation is served from those blocks until the handoff's classifyBlocksAfterMark re-queues them - the cursor serves only virgin blocks created after t0 (threaded-gc-05a). threaded-gc-06 (HEAP_067): inside a parallel minor each worker has one cursor per class. With one worker it adopts the mutator's cursor_[] (the exact reference). With N > 1 the workers share ONE current block per class and claim chunks of it (units of 64 cells, so a chunk owns whole 64-bit bitmap words - the unit bitscan::loadWord reads, whole bytes would not be enough (CR-022) - a claim growing 1 to 16 units per worker per minor) by CAS on a per-class word, the shared block obeys IM13, at the merge it becomes the mutator's cursor again and blocks retired with cells left in a worker's last chunk are re-queued at the FRONT of partial_[class]. Worker cursors exist only between beginParallelPromotion and endParallelPromotion. Outside that window at most one cursor per class exists. Rungs 2-8 of the ladder run under the promotion mutex, and a sweep that completes inside a multi-worker promotion defers onSweepComplete to the merge. threaded-gc-07 (HEAP_070): a block in alloc_state kAllocTenure is owned by one tenure job from grant to merge. The grant takes partial_ front blocks (never the mutator's Current cursor block, which classifyBlocksAfterMark can queue) then virgin blocks, and returns blocks with free cells to the FRONT of partial_ in grant order. Inside a parallel minor with N > 1 workers, allocateFromEmptyRegularBlocks flips nothing (CR-016, plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 3.4, 2026-09-30): chunks and stashes are invisible to it, so live_bytes == 0 is not a fact there, and allocateLargeBlock takes a free large block or a fresh one. With N = 1 the flip stays (no stash, no chunks, and the worker flushes before it retires a block, the Current skip still applies). M4 ReleasedSafe, mutant flip_in_parallel.

THE MIXED-BLOCK LAZY SWEEP READS ONLY LIVE HEADERS (plans/threaded-gc-02-bitmap-allocation.md). With old_gen_bitmap_alloc, lazySweep over a mixed block walks its set mark bits (bitscan::nextSetBit), which are exactly its live objects (marking set them - nothing allocates into an unswept block - startMark cleared stale ones), reads each live object's header only to step over it, clears its bit, and flushes each maximal gap between live objects as one coalesced free run (pushCoalescedFreeCell). It never reads a dead object. work_done still counts span bytes covered, so the pacing knobs keep their units. After a block completes, a header walk over [start, end_of_objects) parses exactly (validator V11), walked when the block completes, or, for a block completed inside a parallel promotion with N > 1, in endParallelPromotion after the join and the stash return (CR-028, plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 4.4, 2026-09-30: a worker may still be writing a cell it popped from the block). Inside a parallel promotion the gap sweep's plain word reads and clearBit on the block under the cursor are exclusive under promo_mu_: a free cell of a block that is not fully_swept (while gc_phase_ == Sweeping: OldGenSpace::cellInUnsweptBlock) is finalized before promo_mu_ is released and is never stashed

description: DEAD NURSERY-OWNED LARGE BODIES ARE RETIRED AT MARK END (plans/threaded-gc-02-bitmap-allocation.md). large_body_index_ holds only nursery-owned bodies (promoteLargeHeader erases promoted ones). With old_gen_bitmap_alloc - where neither the gap sweep nor the bitmap cursor reads dead headers - classifyBlocksAfterMark first runs retireDeadLargeBodies: every entry whose body lies in a non-large block and is unmarked is erased and its large_bodies_ slot's body_base cleared (the id is not recycled, exactly as the former header sweep did), before any cell can be reused. Bodies in is_large blocks are retired by the eager is_large decision in the same function. Otherwise a later sweepNurseryLargeBodies -> freeLargeBodyCell would free a reclaimed cell a second time (validator V12). With an incremental cycle (HEAP_063) retirement runs at the handoff, after the deferred frees of HEAP_026. CR-035 (plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 3.3, 2026-09-30): allocateFromEmptyRegularBlocks retires every index entry inside the flipped block (retireIndexRange, the same retire semantics: erase, body_base cleared, id NOT recycled) before placing the new object at its start, so no stale key can later be erased by a dead meta's free (validate: the Class-4 post-check, message 'flip'). M8 IndexFaithful / NoLostObject, mutant flip_keeps_index.

A MAJOR GC IS ALSO TRIGGERED BY ALLOCATION AGAINST A GROWTH-BOUNDED LIVE SET (plans/threaded-gc-02-bitmap-allocation.md §9 item 7, 2026-09-25). The garbage-fraction trigger ((allocated - post-sweep live) / committed >= major_gc_garbage_fraction) sizes the heap at about gf/(1-gf)+1 times the live set seen at ONE instant, so a major landing on a transient live-set peak sizes the next cycle for the peak (measured: legacy 4-7 majors and 8.8-16.2 GB old-gen peak across gf 0.65-0.75). evaluateMajorGCTrigger therefore also returns LiveBudget when bytes allocated since the last major reach major_gc_live_budget x min(L_i, live_growth_bound x L_{i-1}), where L_i is the mark-derived live set recorded by finalizeMetaAfterMark (major_live_, prev_major_live_). Defaults k = 3.0 (4.5 until 2026-09-29, gc-opt-loop row LB3), r = 1.5, and 0 disables each (RESOLVED 2026-09-29: the k = 3.0 validate failure was not LiveBudget's - its majors only exposed a region-nursery YLOS address-reuse bug (register CR-034), fixed as HEAP_072, and a negative control that relied on a later cycle (CR-030), now caught at the merge (HEAP_051)
source: the validate gate passes at k = 3.0, and the policy-only claim below stands). Both allocator modes. In bitmap mode the garbage-fraction denominator may be capped at garbage_denom_cap x committed at the last major (default 0 = uncapped: the cap only added a major once LiveBudget bounds the peak). Policy, not correctness: every value is safe. With incremental_mark (HEAP_063), L_i is the bytes the cycle's marker TRACED (allocate-black bytes excluded, equal to total live for a STW major), and no trigger is evaluated while a cycle is active (threaded-gc-05a). threaded-gc-05c Part B (HEAP_066): paced by default (major_gc_live_budget_paced - fires when alloc_since_major + H_c * P_hat >= k * live_ref) and the garbage fraction optionally demoted to a backstop (major_gc_garbage_backstop).

description: EVERY GC POLICY DECISION IS INDEPENDENT OF HELPER-THREAD PROGRESS (plans/threaded-gc-03-helper-threads.md, 2026-09-25
source: report design_docs/parallel-gc.md §10). Collection triggers, promotion, nursery sizing, which block or extent an allocation receives, and heap growth and shrink are functions of mutator allocation and of state observed at a mutator sync point, never of how far a helper job got. Mutator code may inspect a helper job only to WAIT for it (a stall), never to choose between outcomes
column7: only GCHelperPool and PageWork read HelperJob::state. gc_thread_mode 1 (sync: jobs run inline at their post point) is the reference: mode 2 (concurrent) and mode 2 with ECO_GC_HELPER_JITTER_US must reproduce its GC counters exactly (unit test testDecommitModesAgreeOnCounters
column8: self-compile gate G8). The incremental mark cycle's schedule (HEAP_063) is fixed at t0: slice budgets are a deterministic function of the previous cycle's units, and the handoff is at minor t0 + T + 1 regardless of mark progress, except a pressure finish (occupancy at a sync point) or a join (threaded-gc-05a). threaded-gc-05b (HEAP_064): the number of markers and their scheduling never affect a decision - units are exact tickets, so every counter is identical at every gc_mark_threads and under ECO_GC_HELPER_JITTER_US. threaded-gc-05c (HEAP_065): background-marking progress (finishedApprox, consumed tickets, markWorkApprox) may decide only pause-internal work (whether and how much to assist, when to merge counters, relaunching a stopped episode), never a trigger, the schedule, allocation or the tail. Every decision counter and the units of every cycle are identical at conc_mark 0/1/2, every B and under ECO_GC_HELPER_JITTER_US (E1). Part B pacing (HEAP_066) reads only mutator allocation. threaded-gc-06 (HEAP_067): with gc_minor_threads > 1, WHICH old-gen cell or to-space address a copy receives depends on the copy schedule. Object-level quantities (every minor's survived/promoted counts and bytes, per-tag totals, the object-byte trigger and nursery growth of HEAP_068, objects allocated) are identical at every gc_minor_threads and under ECO_GC_HELPER_JITTER_US. Decisions that read old-gen placement (committed bytes in GlobalPressure/Headroom/the garbage-fraction denominator, per-block live fractions for demotion/release/compaction, allocated_bytes via path-dependent charges) are schedule-dependent at N > 1 and are judged by distribution (plan E7), not identity. No decision reads worker progress: the per-minor worker choice reads only object bytes and configuration. gc_minor_threads = 1 runs the serial Cheney path and is the exact reference. threaded-gc-07 (HEAP_069/HEAP_070): the tenure job's inputs (start set, heal list, grant, YLOS snapshot) are fixed in the hand-over pause and its outputs merge at the next pause in both tenure modes. Collector progress (finishedApprox) may decide only whether the pause waits or helps and with how many workers. With gc_minor_threads = 1 and the exact engine (tenure_collector_threads = 1), tenure_mode 1 and 2 are bit-identical in every counter, placement and decision, under ECO_GC_HELPER_JITTER_US and forced stops. Against the legacy nursery every object counter is identical (tenured counts one minor later, P§3.18), while old-gen placement and the major sequence may differ and are judged by distribution. With tenure_collector_threads > 1 placement is schedule-dependent (layout class). Per process = per heap under HEAP_007 (one live mutator per process, CR-012 option F, 2026-10-01): with the multi-mutator opt-in (benchmark driver, test harnesses) decisions may read other heaps' shared state and are not deterministic per heap (won't-fix). CR-007 (register-fixes 6.3, 2026-10-01): the no-wait acquire policy of a promotion holder with n > 1 reads only pending_ membership, the free-list order, the bump and n, so modes 1, 2 and 2+jitter stay identical in every counter including the nowait_* ones. Mode 0 (no PageWork, no policy) then differs from them at N > 1 in placement counters only (fresh, reuse, hiwater), and testDecommitModesAgreeOnCounters compares it on object-level quantities there. Explicit collections (HEAP_076, plans/frontend-heap-release.md 2026-10-01) are mutator-chosen sync points, and report observations never feed decisions.

description: EVERY PIN IN test/tla/manifest.txt MATCHES THE CODE IT PINS, AND EVERY HASH CHANGE IS JUSTIFIED BY AN AUDIT.md ENTRY IN EVERY MODEL THAT NAMES IT (plans/threaded-gc-tla-verification.md section 7, 2026-09-29). The TLA+ models of the threaded GC's concurrent protocols (test/tla/M1..M7) and the weak-memory drivers (test/genmc: W1-W5, w_pool_done, w_running_chain) each describe specific C++ code, the manifest pins that code as whole files, TLA-REGION(<id>) begin/end regions (comments stripped, whitespace collapsed), per-file censuses of every atomic/memory-order/lock line in runtime/src/allocator, and the footprint rows' re-derivation greps (test/tla/footprint-greps.txt: the 05c H1-H15, 06 P6.M1-M17 and 07 T1-T11 audit rows plus canary greps). test/scripts/check-tla-manifest.sh runs in ALL (target tla-canary, about a second, only when an input changed) and fails when a pin's hash changes, when a TLA-REGION marker is unpinned or unpaired, when a model in test/tla/models.txt (or a driver family in test/genmc/drivers.txt) has no pin or a pin names an unknown model, when a footprint row appears in no model's MAPPING.md outside the generated pin list, or when an allocator file with a concurrency line has no census pin. --update refuses a changed hash until every named model's AUDIT.md quotes the new hash's first 12 hex digits: the re-audit verdict (no model change needed, or model updated and tla-check re-run) is written before the manifest accepts the code. ECO_TLA_CANARY=warn reports without failing, for work in progress, gates run strict. Same shape as LSS_022's kernel license manifest: a guard that only checked hashes would let new concurrency code arrive unguarded, hence the coverage checks.

GC HELPER JOBS ARE POSTED ONLY AT MUTATOR SLOW PATHS AND COLLECTED ONLY AT ALLOCATOR SLOW PATHS (plans/threaded-gc-03-helper-threads.md). Posts happen at the outermost pause end (ThreadLocalHeap PauseEndHook -> Allocator::onGCPauseEnd, the sync point) and waits in acquireOldGenBlock / releaseOldGenBlock, all under Allocator::thread_mutex_. The waiter is the mutator or (threaded-gc-06/07, CR-026) a GCMarkGang member inside a minor pause that holds promo_mu_ (the parallel minor's virgin-block and bag-page rungs, a sweep completing in a mutex rung, the pause tenure engine) - such a wait is a pause stall (Allocator::callerInPause counts a running gang member as in the pause, CR-025). description: WITH HeapConfig::incremental_mark A MAJOR GC IS A MARK CYCLE SPANNING T + 1 MINOR GCS (plans/threaded-gc-05a-incremental-marking.md, 2026-09-26, T = incremental_mark_slices, requires old_gen_bitmap_alloc). The cycle starts at the end of the minor GC that fires a major trigger (t0): in that pause the old-gen targets of every root and off-heap store (HEAP_SNAPSHOT_002) and of every young object (dead survivors are zapped: HEAP_070 merge, HEAP_074 major) - the nursery's survivor prefix [fromBase, bump_.ptr), exact only until the mutator allocates (NurserySpace::forEachSurvivor asserts bump_.ptr == survivor_end_), and every YLOS object (HEAP_062) - are greyed with pushMarkRoot in snapshot mode (young targets dropped), and every YLOS cell is marked. After t0 the marker never reads a root or a young object (validator IM3). Slices of paced mark work (max(incremental_mark_min_slice_units, remaining predicted units / slices left)) run at the next T - 1 minor ends, the T-th minor end drains the mark stack (closing slice), and the post-mark tail (the handoff: resetAllocCursors, then OldGenSpace::runPostMarkTail) runs at the (T + 1)-th. The schedule is fixed at t0 (GC_DET_001), except an emergency finish when old-gen committed / cap >= incremental_mark_finish_fraction, or a join when majorGC() is called during a cycle (which finishes the cycle, then runs the requested stop-the-world major). While a cycle is active: gc_phase_ == Marking, every old-gen allocation is allocated black (mark bit set, bytes in BufferMetadata::live_bytes), the uniform cursor serves only blocks created after t0 (HEAP_054), no block is released, no body or YLOS cell is freed (HEAP_026 deferral), no compaction runs, and the major triggers are suppressed. Soundness rests on HEAP_005, HEAP_SNAPSHOT_001 and HEAP_SNAPSHOT_002: every object reachable at the handoff was reachable at t0 (and is marked) or was allocated after t0 (and is black). Validators IM1-IM9 (ECO_HEAP_VALIDATE) re-derive it: IM1/IM2 are independent reachability traces checked at the handoff, IM4 checks every in-cycle allocation is black and never lands on a marked cell. One cycle counts as one major. threaded-gc-05b: slice, closing, pressure and join mark work may run on N markers (HEAP_064), cycle units are exact tickets counted in OldGenSpace::runMarkers. The t0 snapshot never chunks (young objects are scanned completely at t0). threaded-gc-05c: with conc_mark = 2 the slices become paced ASSISTS into a running background episode (HEAP_065) and the closing step joins that episode until termination. Kind-4 pauses occur only when an assist or a closing join ran. Schedule, marked set and units per cycle are unchanged. threaded-gc-07 (HEAP_069/HEAP_070): in region mode the t0 young walk (NurserySpace::forEachYoung) covers the Fresh extent (survivors and builders) and the Tenuring extent, then YLOS, and IM7 is 'eden is empty'. The tenure job is built after the cycle decision (the scope-exit launch), so its copies are allocate-black mid-cycle and its grant holds only post-t0 blocks. A STW major joins the tenure job first and greys the copy of every forwarded Tenuring object it reaches. IM5's key includes the id's BlockTable generation, so a same-id, same-start re-issue is caught (CR-036, plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 3.5, 2026-09-30).

WITH gc_mark_threads > 1 THE OLD-GEN MARK WORK OF AN INCREMENTAL CYCLE (HEAP_063: SLICES, CLOSING DRAIN, PRESSURE FINISH, JOIN DRAIN) RUNS ON N MARKERS (plans/threaded-gc-05b-parallel-marking.md, 2026-09-26): the paused mutator as marker 0 and N-1 GCMarkGang threads, started and joined inside the pause (0 = auto: min(gc_mark_threads_cap, affinity/cgroup CPUs), ECO_GC_MARK_THREADS wins over JSON, 1 = serial). Default gc_mark_threads = 0 (auto) with cap 16 (experiments E2/E3). Grey entries are 8-byte markwork entries (address >> 3 plus block id + 1, or a chunk index). Each marker pushes and pops on a PRIVATE stack (owner-only, no atomics) and publishes its oldest half to its Chase-Lev deque (MarkWork.hpp, the PPoPP 2013 C11 orders, old arrays freed only after the join) when the deque is empty, thieves steal only from deques, and each marker's private size is visible to the termination check through a relaxed atomic. Mark bits and large-mark bytes are set with atomic fetch_or / exchange, and each marker attributes live bytes only to its own LiveBytesAccumulator, merged in index order (HEAP_051). Work is accounted in exact tickets: an entry is taken from an own or a stolen deque only with a ticket in hand, rings always drain, and idle markers hold no tickets, so the units a slice consumes are min(budget, entries available) independent of N and scheduling (GC_DET_001). A slice ends when all markers are idle (spin, yield, then sleep while idle): the active count, a reactivation epoch and the done flag share one 64-bit word, and done is committed by a CAS from the exact word in which the decider saw zero active markers, so a reactivation between its checks makes the commit fail. Boxed Tag_Array and Tag_ListBacking ranges over MARK_CHUNK_ELEMS are scanned as chunk entries, except in the t0 snapshot. The legacy STW majorGC (nursery traversal via nursery_visited_) stays serial, a parallel marker aborts on a nursery pointer, and with incremental_mark off and N > 1 trigger majors run as T = 0 cycles. Validators IM10 (each entry scanned once), IM11 (the scanned set equals the old-gen closure of the t0 grey set) and IM12 (entries scanned = tickets consumed). threaded-gc-05c (HEAP_065): markers occupy SLOTS 0..F-1 (foreground, F = gc_mark_threads) and F..F+B-1 (background) and the victim range is all slots. Every exit of a parallel run publishes its private stack (IM15 - no private work between runs). Deque arrays are retired only when no run and no background episode is active. Participants are Members (idle until termination) or Assists (bounded ticket pool, never idle, leave after publishing) and a joiner enters a running control through reactivate(). threaded-gc-06: GCMarkGang also runs parallel minor workers (HEAP_067) and is sized for max(gc_mark_threads, gc_minor_threads) (OldGenSpace::ensureGang).

WITH conc_mark = 2 THE OLD-GEN MARK WORK OF AN INCREMENTAL CYCLE (HEAP_063, T >= 1) RUNS ON B BACKGROUND MARKERS OUTSIDE GC PAUSES (plans/threaded-gc-05c-concurrent-marking.md, 2026-09-27): per-heap GCBackgroundGang threads at conc_mark_priority (set once per thread - an unprivileged process cannot raise it again), launched at the end of the t0 pause with the t0 grey set distributed round-robin over their deques, marking while the mutator runs Elm code and minor GCs. They read only S_H objects (frozen by HEAP_SNAPSHOT_001), the t0 MarkView, page-index slots and BlockInfo published by release/acquire (HEAP_049), and mark bytes (atomic). They write only mark bytes (atomic) and their own slot. The mutator touches a slot's owner-only state only while no thread runs on it (IM14). At minor ends 1..T-1 the paused mutator and the foreground gang may JOIN the running episode for a bounded assist (budget from a deterministic lagged schedule, conc_mark_assist_lag - pause-only). At k = T they join as Members until termination, and pressure finishes and joins do the same. The handoff at k = T + 1 is unchanged. A stopped episode (fork prepare, reset) leaves all work in deques and is relaunched at the next step. FORK, STOP, CLOSING (plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 7.2 steps 4-6, 2026-10-01): a launch while a fork's prepare holds the gang (fork_hold_, set under each gang's m_ BEFORE stopAllForFork) is REFUSED, never blocked, and treated as a stopped episode (launchBackground leaves bg_ep_ None

description: HEAP-RELATIVE TRIGGER PACING (plans/threaded-gc-05c-concurrent-marking.md P§3.11, Part B). P_hat is the integer EWMA (1/8 per minor) of the old-gen bytes allocated between minor ends, from the monotone OldGenSpace::old_alloc_total_ (incremented next to every allocated_bytes += and never lowered by sweeps). H_c = T + 1 minors (the fixed cycle schedule, HEAP_063). Headroom (major_gc_headroom_margin > 0): a cycle starts when old-gen committed + margin * H_c * P_hat >= incremental_mark_finish_fraction * cap. Paced LiveBudget (major_gc_live_budget_paced): alloc_since_major + H_c * P_hat >= k * live_ref. Backstop (major_gc_garbage_backstop > 0 with LiveBudget on): the garbage-fraction threshold is max(gf, backstop). Defaults (05c E9/E10): Headroom ON with margin 1.5, paced LiveBudget ON (it cut the gf-sweep peak spread 44.5 % to 6.4 % for up to +2 majors that cost no pause time under concurrent marking) and backstop OFF (rejected). All inputs are mutator allocation and occupancy at a minor end and nothing reads collector progress (GC_DET_001).

WITH gc_minor_threads > 1 THE COPY PHASE OF A MINOR GC RUNS ON N WORKERS (plans/threaded-gc-06-parallel-minor.md, 2026-09-27): the paused mutator as worker 0 and N-1 GCMarkGang threads, started and joined inside the minor pause. The root phase stays serial on worker 0 and its greys are distributed round-robin. A from-space object is copied exactly once: a worker CASes its header word from the observed header to BUSY (Tag_Forward, forward_ptr 0), sizes the object from the SAVED header, copies the body, writes the copy's header from the saved word (age/colour as the serial evacuate), then publishes the forward word (Tag_Forward, the original colour, the address) with a release store. Readers load headers with acquire and wait out BUSY. Young survivors go to per-worker to-space LABs claimed from an atomic top (objects >= lab/4, and those that do not fit a LAB with more than lab/64 left, are claimed directly, and a retired LAB tail becomes a Tag_Free filler). Promoted objects go to per-worker AllocCursors over chunks of a shared per-class block (HEAP_054) or, below rung 1, under the promotion spin lock (rung-2 free cells popped in batches of 16 and finalized outside it). Grey entries are markwork entries in per-worker private stacks and Chase-Lev deques driven by markwork::runMarkerLoop with kDrainBudget, and an idle worker wakes only for stealable (deque) work. List spines are copied in runs of MINOR_SPINE_RUN with a heads pass that COUNTS cells, and boxed arrays and list backings over MINOR_CHUNK_ELEMS are chunked. Large-body index updates are deferred to worker 0 after the join (promote-all, then mark-seen), and YLOS reaches run under a mutex. A minor runs parallel only when S + (S / (lab - lab/64) + N) * lab/64 + N * lab <= capacity (S = from-space object bytes) and S >= minor_parallel_min_bytes, else serially. gc_minor_threads = 1 runs the serial Cheney path unchanged. Default gc_minor_threads = 0 (auto, cap 8). Validators PM1-PM6 (exactly-once, no stale from-space slot, filler accounting, cursor discipline, old-parent/young-child, allocator accounting). Every completion of lazySweep inside a parallel promotion (in-loop or tail, via lazySweep's completeSweep) goes through sweepCompleteInPromotion: with N > 1 onSweepComplete is deferred to endParallelPromotion after the join and the stash return

description: THE NURSERY SURVIVOR PREFIX MAY CONTAIN FILLERS, AND NURSERY POLICY COUNTS OBJECT BYTES (plans/threaded-gc-06-parallel-minor.md P§3.5, 2026-09-27). A parallel minor turns LAB tails into Tag_Free fillers (header.size = bytes) inside the to-space prefix, and NurserySpace::filler_bytes_ records the fillers of the from-space survivor prefix. The minor-GC trigger (computeAllocEnd: end = base + threshold + fillers, capped at the extent and counted as alloc_end_capped), the fail-soft test, nursery growth (checkAndGrow), isNurseryNearFull and the minor stats use object bytes = prefix bytes - filler bytes. Every survivor-prefix walker skips Tag_Free (forEachSurvivor, the P1 census). At gc_minor_threads = 1 there are no fillers and every formula is the pre-phase-6 one. threaded-gc-07 (HEAP_069): in region mode the survived object bytes S_m of the last minor (fill survivor objects plus builders, fillers excluded) play the survivor prefix's role: eden's allotment is threshold - S_m (fail-soft capacity - S_m), objectBytesAllocated = S_m + eden bytes, growth reads S_m / capacity.

WITH nursery_regions = 1 THE NURSERY IS AN EDEN AND THREE SURVIVOR EXTENTS (plans/threaded-gc-07-concurrent-tenuring.md, 2026-09-27). A heap owns n extents (4, or 5 with eden flip - the default in ECO_HEAP_VALIDATE builds) of one capacity, contiguous at a power-of-two stride in its slot block (HEAP_042). Minor m evacuates eden completely on phase 6's engine (header claim/publish, LABs, fillers): non-builders into the Free survivor extent (which becomes Fresh, holding G_m, age 1), builders into that extent's top-down builder area (age 0). References into the Fresh extent of the previous minor (now Hand, G_{m-1}) are recorded without a header load: root, builder and hand-over-YLOS targets in the start set S_m, slots of survivor copies and of young non-builder YLOS objects in the heal list H_m. References into the Tenuring extent of the previous minor (now Retire, G_{m-2}, whose live objects the tenure job promoted) are resolved through that extent's shadow (TV1: a miss aborts in every build), and H_{m-1} is healed at the minor's start. Retire is then unreferenced and becomes Free (poisoned 0xDD in validate builds). At most three survivor extents are non-Free (TV10). Eden's allotment is threshold minus the object bytes survived at the previous minor (fail-soft capacity minus them), which makes every trigger, growth decision and object counter equal the legacy nursery's, and a fill cannot overflow. Every nursery object has a size class: the large-pointer nursery cap is clamped to the largest old-gen size class, allocateFast refuses larger requests, and validate() requires large_object_threshold <= the largest class + 8. promotion_age must be 1 and old_gen_bitmap_alloc on. nursery_regions = 0 is the legacy nursery unchanged. DEFAULT (2026-09-28, TG7d): nursery_regions = 2 (auto) resolves when the Allocator adopts a config - to 1 when regionIncompatibility() is empty (promotion_age 1, bitmap allocation, a size class for every nursery object, room for one heap slot), to 0 otherwise - and tenure_mode = 2 with one collector. An explicit 1 still rejects an incompatible config. TENURE AGEING (2026-09-28, threaded-gc-07b, plans/threaded-gc-07b-tenure-ageing.md): the tenure age k is promotion_age (1..3). A heap owns k + 2 survivor extents (n = k + 3, +1 with eden flip). At minor m the Young extent of age k is the hand-over (Hand), younger Young extents are Age (a reference into one is recorded as a mark source, never healed), the age-1 extent's builder area is PrevBuilders and Tenuring is Retire. At the end every Young extent ages by one. Between minors every non-free object of a survivor extent was copied at the last minor or was marked live by the last hand-over job, and was reached by every STW major since (amended 2026-09-30, CR-017: HEAP_074): the merge after each hand-over turns every unmarked ageing object into a Tag_Free filler (the zap), a region-mode STW major zaps every Young extent's survivor it did not reach (HEAP_074), and the merge clears the slots of the ageing-generation YLOS its mark did not reach (HEAP_070, CR-038), so no walker reads a dead object's slots (TV2Y). YLOS objects and large bodies of ageing generations are re-coloured every minor until their generation is handed over.

THE LIVE OBJECTS OF THE TENURING EXTENT ARE PROMOTED BY A TENURE JOB (plans/threaded-gc-07-concurrent-tenuring.md, 2026-09-27), built at the end of the hand-over minor after the cycle decision (a scope-exit launch on every return path of ThreadLocalHeap::minorGC) and merged at the start of the next minor, of a STW major, or at teardown / exit (stats only). It promotes exactly the objects reachable from S_m U *H_m through the extent (and generation YLOS reached through it), recording forwarding in the extent's shadow (one 64-bit word per granule of 2^shadow_granule_log2 bytes - 16 by default since 2026-09-29

description: LIVE BYTES OF A NON-LARGE BLOCK ARE AN UPPER BOUND OUTSIDE THE MARK WINDOW (plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 3.2, 2026-09-30, CR-018, CR-001). Outside [resetBufferMetaForMark, finalizeMetaAfterMark], BufferMetadata::live_bytes of a non-large block is >= the bytes of every object allocated into it since the last mark. Every allocator writer adds in EVERY phase, not only while marking_active or gc_phase_ != Idle: initObjectHeaderWithSize (free-list pop, split, bag-page carve - any cell_bytes > 0), finalizePoppedCellW (the parallel stash finalize, a relaxed atomic fetch_add in every phase) and flushCursor/flushCursorW (the cursor's pending_live). The add is a relaxed atomic_ref fetch_add while the cell is black or a parallel promotion is active (par_promo_active_: other workers add lock-free), and a plain owner add otherwise. The allocate-black colour and mark bit stay gated on the phase. freeLargeBodyCell's clamped subtraction removes only bytes that were added (its cell_size never exceeds the bytes the allocation counted). Readers that treat live_bytes == 0 as empty rely on it: the empty-regular-block flip (allocateFromEmptyRegularBlocks), the shrink passes 1 and 2 (maybeShrinkCapacity) and the reclaim. resetBufferMetaForMark zeroes live_bytes at every mark, and V8/IM6 check only uniform blocks (exact: popcount x cell), where no free-list cell lies in bitmap mode. Without it a mixed block refilled after its sweep read fully_swept and live_bytes == 0, and an exact-page allocation flipped it to large over live objects (CR-018, S1), and a stash cell finalized at Idle left its block releasable by the deferred shrink (CR-001's S1 half). Checked by the TLA+ models M8 (NoOverwriteLive, FlipTrustsTruth, mutant idle_uncounted) and M4 (ReleasedSafe, mutant idle_uncounted_release). Negative-control hook: OldGenSpace::test_idle_uncounted_ (OldGenSpaceTestAccess::setIdleUncounted).

IN REGION MODE A STW MAJOR, AFTER ITS MARK, TURNS EVERY SURVIVOR-PART OBJECT OF EVERY YOUNG EXTENT THAT IT DID NOT REACH (nursery_visited_) INTO TAG_FREE FILLERS, BEFORE THE MUTATOR RESUMES (plans/threaded-gc-register-fixes.md 5.2, 2026-09-30, CR-017). NurserySpace::zapDeadAfterMajor runs in ThreadLocalHeap::majorGC right after finishMarkAndSweep (OldGenSpace::majorReachedNursery is valid from the mark end until the next prepareMark), coalesces each maximal dead run into one filler (validate builds poison the rest with 0xD8), and never runs inside a minor or with the tenure job unmerged (it aborts). The Tenuring extent (merged at the major's tenureJoin, retiring at the next minor, resolveRetire and the heal still read its forwarded originals) and builder areas (kernels hold builders) are not touched, eden is empty at t0 (IM7). It covers every Young extent, ages 1..k: at k = 1 the extent handed over at the next minor, at k >= 2 also the ageing extents, which t0 reads before their first ageing mark. Consequence: no object that forEachYoung walks has a slot naming a cell freed by a major, so the t0 young walk never greys a freed old cell (CR-017: floating garbage, IM4/IM6 aborts, and a marker scanning a reallocated YLOS). Premise: the major's young reachability is a superset of the minor's (the root enumerations minorGCRegion and collectRoots + forEachMajorRoot are the same set, HEAP_SNAPSHOT_001 keeps a survivor's slots frozen), and no runtime code holds an unrooted reference to a survivor across majorGC (HeapHelpers Pattern 1, allocateYoungLarge / allocateLargePinned run a major only on allocation failure, and every allocation is a GC point). Validate tripwire: evacuateR's Hand and Age cases abort on a Tag_Free (or poisoned) target. Stats: rg.major_zaps, major_zapped, major_zapped_bytes, major_zap_ns, major_zap_ns_max. description: AN EXPLICIT COLLECTION IS A MUTATOR SYNC POINT (plans/frontend-heap-release.md §3, 2026-10-01). Allocator::collectMajorAndRelease runs only from a kernel Task binding (Eco.GC.majorGC) or a test on the owning mutator with pause_depth_ == 0 (fatal otherwise, so no minor, parallel promotion or CR-014 path is active). ThreadLocalHeap::majorGCAndShrink is ONE pause and ONE sync point: its outermost PauseEndHook makes the nested STW major (MajorReason::Explicit, joins the tenure job and finishes any cycle by Join) an inner pause, then OldGenSpace::finishSweepForRelease drives the lazy sweep to Idle and shrinkToFloorForRelease runs maybeShrinkCapacity(ShrinkPass::Forced), which releases every fully-swept live_bytes == 0 block and unassigned page down to max(initial_old_gen_size, alloc_buffer_size) with no hysteresis (passes 1-3 unchanged, kAllocTenure skipped), and does nothing during a cycle, an unfinished sweep or a compaction. After the pause, under thread_mutex_ only (TLA-REGION AL.releaseDiscard), PageWork::drainAll(decommitOn()) waits for every slot and discards every Pending extent (with decommit off nothing is Pending and nothing is discarded), in mode 0 releases were already discarded inline. malloc_trim(0) (glibc) runs after the lock is released. No collection or shrink step holds thread_mutex_ (HEAP_075), pool workers never take it (HEAP_058). The drain is a mutator step outside any pause, so no extent is reused while it runs and HEAP_059 holds (M7 DiscardAllPending). Modes 1 and 2 agree in every decision counter (GC_DET_001): the call adds one sync epoch and one Allocator major epoch, and drainAll empties pending_ identically. Allocator::collectMinor is a plain minorGC (it may chain into a major) with the same snapshots. GCReport (runtime/src/allocator/GCReport.hpp) rss_*, *_ns and trim_result are observations, no GC policy or Elm control flow may read them, and the nursery is not decommitted (v1). NO COLLECTOR THREAD WRITES AN OBJECT HEADER OR FIELD THAT THE MUTATOR CAN READ (plans/threaded-gc-07-concurrent-tenuring.md P§3.22, report design_docs/parallel-gc.md §11.2, broadened, 2026-09-27). Concurrent forwarding lives off-header (the survivor-extent shadow, HEAP_070), and the heal of recorded slots happens in a pause. A collector thread writes only memory no mutator path can reach until a later pause publishes it (its own fresh copies in granted blocks, shadow words, job-private state).
